"The vessel stopped without further incident," JIATF-S said.

During follow-on operations, Coast Guard crews discovered what officials described as a "bale field" along the vessel's prior track and recovered the suspected marijuana, valued at more than $2.4 million.
"This mission required vigilance, professionalism, and seamless coordination from detection and pursuit to evidence recovery and search-and-rescue support," JIATF-S said.
WHITE HOUSE HIGHLIGHTS 'STEEPEST' EVER DECLINE IN US CASUALTIES FROM CARTELS AMID BOAT STRIKES

JIATF-S did not specify where the incident took place, but thanked the Coast Guard Cutter Escanaba and Joint Rescue Coordination Center Haiti for their "timely support, search assistance, and coordination throughout the operation."
The drug seizure comes amid the Trump administration's ongoing campaign targeting narcotics trafficking networks in the Western Hemisphere.
U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) touted the operation, saying the "bust is another demonstration of the United States' resolve to stop the flow of dangerous drugs into the homeland."

This week, SOUTHCOM said it conducted two operations in which U.S. forces intercepted and sank vessels in the Eastern Pacific that the military said were tied to Los Choneros, which it described as a violent narco-terrorist organization.
US KILLS TWO 'NARCO-TERRORISTS' IN STRIKE 2 MONTHS SINCE LAST ANNOUNCED ANTI-'NARCO-TRAFFICKING' ATTACK

title: Lindsay Clancy jury wraps day 6 with bombshell one-juror standoff, deliberations to resume Friday
summary: Lindsay Clancy’s jury ended its sixth day without a verdict after a dispute involving a holdout juror, with deliberations set to resume Friday.
story: Fox News national correspondent Bryan Llenas reports as jury deliberations enter a sixth day in the Lindsay Clancy trial and questions emerge over whether the panel can reach a unanimous verdict. Llenas details defense attorney Kevin Reddington’s claim that one juror is refusing to follow the law on reasonable doubt and the latest developments from the courtroom on ‘The Story.’
The jury deciding Lindsay Clancy’s fate ended a dramatic sixth day of deliberations Thursday without a verdict amid a dispute involving a holdout juror, with deliberations set to resume Friday.

The panel of nine women and three men has twice reported being deadlocked. Jurors are expected to return Friday, when Judge William Sullivan is also set to address a dispute involving one member of the panel.

Earlier Thursday, defense attorney Kevin Reddington unsuccessfully sought to remove a juror after the foreperson reported that the person was refusing to follow the court’s instructions on reasonable doubt.
Reddington warned that the case could end without a verdict because of a juror who had "spurned the instructions" of the court.
LINDSAY CLANCY JURY RECAP: DAY 5 ENDS WITH NO VERDICT AFTER RARE INSTRUCTION

Lindsay Clancy and Kevin Reddington listen to Judge Sullivan ask the jury to continue deliberations during Clancy's murder trial on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via AP, Pool)

Prosecutors objected to removing anyone, arguing there was no way to determine who was right or wrong without improperly examining the jury’s private deliberations. They said Sullivan had acted appropriately by questioning the jurors about whether they could follow the law and again instructing them on reasonable doubt.
WHAT IS A TUEY-RODRIGUEZ CHARGE? JUDGE GIVES INSTRUCTION TO DEADLOCKED LINDSAY CLANCY JURY
Sullivan declined, calling the removal of a deliberating juror "a sensitive undertaking" and saying the court could not take sides in the jury’s deliberations.
After court, Reddington revealed that a later jury note appeared to show an 11-to-1 divide.
SOCIAL MEDIA IS LINDSAY CLANCY WILD CARD THAT COULD TILT POTENTIAL RETRIAL TO THE DEFENSE, RETIRED JUDGE SAYS

Kevin J. Reddington addresses the media outside of Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., on Thursday, September 3, 2026. His client, Lindsay Clancy, is on trial for the murder of her three children in 2023. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
"When a note that the judge already has says that there are 11 jurors that have made a decision and one juror will not apply reasonable [doubt]... ," Reddington said.
The note does not reveal which verdict the 11 jurors favor or how the remaining juror is leaning.
HARVEY WEINSTEIN RAPE TRIAL ENDS IN MISTRIAL AFTER JURY DEADLOCKED
The empty Plymouth Superior Court jury box during the Lindsay Clancy murder trial in Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026. (Greg Derr/Pool The Patriot Ledger via AP)
Reddington said Sullivan plans to hold an inquiry at 9 a.m. Friday. If jurors again say they cannot reach a unanimous decision, the case could end in a mistrial.
The defense attorney said he expects the arguments over the jury issue to take place in open court rather than at sidebar.
LINDSAY CLANCY’S FUTURE COULD REST WITH ‘PROSECUTION DOCTORS’ AS CASE ECHOES INFAMOUS MAINE KILLINGS: EXPERT
Asked whether a retrial could favor prosecutors, Reddington issued a blunt response.
"Bring it," he said, adding that his witnesses and evidence are ready.
"I got witnesses lined up. We’re all set. Dr. Resnick is ready. I’m ready. We’ve got all our evidence. Witnesses are available, so let’s go," Reddington said.

Lindsay Clancy's lawyer, Kevin J. Reddington, arrives at Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., on Tuesday, September 1, 2026. Clancy's murder trial enters its fourth day of jury deliberation today. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)

Reddington said prosecutors might seek to put off another trial "for six months or a year," but indicated he would be ready to move quickly. He deferred to Plymouth County District Attorney Timothy Cruz when questioned about the possibility of a plea agreement.
"Let’s see what Mr. Cruz wants to do, and then we’ll talk about our options," Reddington said.

Clancy, 36, faces three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her children, Cora, Dawson and Callan, who were all under the age of 6 when they were found strangled in the family’s Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023.
LINDSAY CLANCY VERDICT: RETIRED JUDGE EXPLAINS WHAT HAPPENS IF INSANITY DEFENSE PREVAILS
Lindsay Clancy looks at jurors as Judge Sullivan asks them to start deliberations for a sixth day during her murder trial on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger)
She does not dispute killing them. Jurors must instead decide whether she was criminally responsible at the time.

Prosecutors argue Clancy understood what she was doing and should be held responsible for the children’s deaths. Her attorneys contend she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and could not appreciate the wrongfulness of her actions or conform her conduct to the law.

The jury is considering several possible outcomes, including first-degree murder, second-degree murder, voluntary or involuntary manslaughter, not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility or not guilty.

title: WATCH: Bystanders, police lift Volkswagen off woman pinned underneath after dramatic e-bike crash
summary: Body camera video captured strangers and officers lifting a Volkswagen Beetle off a trapped e-bike rider after a crash on a Prospect Park road.
story: A police bodycam captured officers and bystanders rushing to lift a Volkswagen Beetle and free a 44-year-old woman who became pinned beneath the car after an e-bike crash in Prospect Park, Pennsylvania. (Credit: WTXF)

A group of strangers and police officers rushed to lift a Volkswagen Beetle off an injured e-bike rider after she became trapped beneath the car during a crash on a busy Pennsylvania road, dramatic body camera video shows.

Local authorities said the 44-year-old woman suffered several broken bones in Monday morning's crash in Prospect Park but survived after roughly six bystanders joined officers to lift the vehicle and pull her to safety, FOX 29 reported.

Prospect Park Police Chief Dave Madonna said the woman was riding an e-bike more than 20 mph, according to his estimate, without a helmet when she collided with the Volkswagen at an intersection along Route 420.

"She was driving way too fast for that time of day, for the road she was traveling on," Madonna said, adding that he believed she had been trying to overtake vehicles while traveling to an appointment.
RESCUERS FREE CLIMBER TRAPPED BENEATH 16,000-POUND BOULDER ON OREGON'S MOUNT HOOD IN COMPLEX OPERATION
Bystanders and police officers work together to lift a Volkswagen Beetle off an e-bike rider who became trapped beneath the vehicle after a crash in Prospect Park, Pa. (WTXF)
Surveillance and police body camera video shows bystanders rushing to the crash to help.
About six people then work together to lift the car high enough to free the woman trapped underneath.
"Got a yell to help, ran over. We lifted the Volkswagen Beetle up, pulled the girl out and pushed her to the ground so she wouldn't move, that's all," FedEx driver Carl Wise told the station.
GOOD SAMARITAN IN SPIDER-MAN COSTUME HELPS MAN IN WHEELCHAIR CROSS BUSY INTERSECTION IN VIRAL MOMENT
Police body camera video shows bystanders rushing to help lift a car off a 44-year-old e-bike rider following a crash along Route 420 in Pennsylvania. (WTXF)
"I'm no hero. I'm just a guy doing a job, that's all," he added.
Local business owner Chrissy Vollmer, who also responded, described what she saw.
"All I saw were the lady's legs underneath the car, and she was just yelling, ‘Get this car off of me,’" Vollmer said.
Madonna called the bystanders who helped rescue the woman "heroes" and later visited them to offer his thanks.
ICE OFFICER HAILED AS HERO AFTER SAVING DRIVER INJURED IN MISSOURI CRASH
About six bystanders joined police officers to lift a Volkswagen Beetle and free a woman trapped underneath, according to local authorities. (WTXF)
He also raised concerns about what he described as an increase in e-bike crashes.
"How many more tragedies do we have to see before some type of action is taken?" Madonna said.
The woman was taken to Lankenau Hospital and underwent surgery for a broken collarbone and other injuries, FOX 29 reported.

The Volkswagen driver is not facing charges, and  police said the e-bike rider could receive a traffic citation pending the outcome of the investigation.

story: Fox News' Chanley Painter has the latest on the response to the crime on 'Fox News @ Night.'
Minnesota officials released the identities of the victims involved in Wednesday’s Minneapolis apartment shooting that left two civilians dead and two police officers injured by gunfire.

The two civilians were Dale Henry Spry, 63, and Muse A. Afrah, 61, according to the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension (BCA). Officials previously said one victim died at the apartment complex and the other died at a hospital.

Both victims are believed to have been residents of the apartment complex where Carlton Neal Johnson II, 35, opened fire before he was fatally struck in an exchange of gunfire with police. A preliminary autopsy indicated Johnson died after sustaining multiple gunshot wounds, and his death was ruled a homicide, officials said.

The two Minneapolis Police Department (MPD) officers injured in the shooting were identified as Joseph Michnowski, a five-year veteran, and Yahye Ahmed, a nearly two-year veteran, according to the BCA.
3 DEAD, INCLUDING SUSPECTED GUNMAN, AND 3 OFFICERS INJURED IN MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING
The suspected gunman in the shooting in downtown Minneapolis reportedly was facing eviction from an apartment building. (Ellen Schmidt/AP)
Ahmed was released from a hospital Thursday, while Michnowski remained hospitalized Thursday afternoon, interim Police Chief Bill Peterson said during a briefing.
Garrett Parten, an MPD public information officer, said one of the injured officers sustained an apparent non-life-threatening gunshot wound to the leg, while the other underwent surgery.
Another officer involved in the incident was also evaluated for an apparent non-life-threatening injury, Parten said.
MINNEAPOLIS APARTMENT SHOOTING SUSPECT WAS FACING EVICTION: REPORT
Officers investigating the aftermath of a shooting in Minneapolis Wednesday. (Ellen Schmidt/AP Photo)

Peterson identified the third officer as Ernest Boateng but clarified that his injuries were not directly related to the gunfire. Boateng was cut by glass while breaking a window of a locked police vehicle whose sirens were going off, Peterson said.
Boateng was evaluated and released Wednesday.
The BCA said at least one officer discharged his gun during the incident, identifying the officer as Liban Mohamed Ibrahim, a two-year MPD veteran.
"Investigators are continuing to determine whether any other officers fired their weapons," BCA said.
Law enforcement responds to a shooting in Minneapolis Wednesday. (Ellen Schmidt/AP Photo)

Wednesday’s shooting began during a domestic child custody exchange involving a woman who previously had a relationship with Johnson, according to Drew Evans, superintendent of the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension.

Johnson reportedly shot the woman outside the building before going inside the apartment, where he shot another facility worker. He then went to the ninth floor, where he shot two residents who later died.
He was also facing eviction from the apartment building, according to court records obtained by Fox9 Minneapolis.

Officials have not determined whether Johnson specifically targeted the victims.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Trump names Adam Telle acting secretary of the Army following Dan Driscoll's resignation
summary: Adam Telle steps in as acting Army secretary after Dan Driscoll's resignation amid reported clashes with Pete Hegseth over Army readiness efforts.
story: Fox News chief national security correspondent Jennifer Griffin discusses Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitting his resignation to President Donald Trump, the reported tensions within Pentagon leadership and the latest developments in the escalating U.S.-Iran conflict, including what the shake-up could mean for America's military strategy and national security on 'America Reports.'
President Donald Trump on Thursday announced he was appointing Adam Telle, assistant secretary of the Army for Civil Works, as acting secretary of the Army.
"I am pleased to announce that Adam Telle, the current Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works, will become Acting Secretary of the Army, effective immediately," Trump posted on Truth Social.
"He is a Great Patriot, who is respected by all."
He made the announcement after Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation to the president earlier this week.
ARMY SECRETARY DAN DRISCOLL SUBMITS RESIGNATION TO TRUMP
President Donald Trump appointed Adam Telle as acting secretary of the Army after the resignation of Army Secretary Dan Driscoll. (Kent Nishimura/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Telle, who was nominated by Trump and confirmed by the Senate in 2025, oversees the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' Civil Works program, where his responsibilities include flood and storm protection, commercial waterways and Clean Water Act permitting.

Previously, Telle served as chief of staff to Sen. Bill Hagerty, R-Tenn., and was Trump's chief liaison to the Senate during the president's first administration, when he led the White House Office of Legislative Affairs' Senate team.

Before that, Telle served on the Senate Appropriations Committee subcommittee responsible for overseeing the Department of Homeland Security's budget. He also spent 10 years in the office of former Sen. Thad Cochran, R-Miss., where he served as deputy chief of staff, legislative director and the senator's top national security staffer.
TRUMP’S ARMY SECRETARY HUNT TAKES SHAPE AS INSIDERS FLOAT POTENTIAL PICKS

U.S. Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll, War Secretary Pete Hegseth and President Donald Trump attend a dignified transfer at Dover Air Force Base for military casualties of the war with Iran July 22, 2026, in Dover, Del. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)
Telle is viewed as having strong relationships with senators on Capitol Hill, which could prove important as the administration works to confirm Army nominees stalled in the Senate.
The appointment fills a key leadership vacancy atop the nation's largest military branch.

Driscoll's exit came after he reportedly butted heads with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth over the Army's transformation and readiness, including Driscoll's belief that Hegseth had hindered those efforts, Fox News Digital previously reported.
US ARMY OFFERING DEFENSE FIRMS 'CONCIERGE ACCESS' TO TEST WEAPONS AT MILITARY RANGES
President Donald Trump announced that Adam Telle would become acting secretary of the Army "effective immediately," calling him a "Great Patriot." (AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein)
The outgoing Army secretary said Wednesday would be his "last full day" in the position, adding that serving under Trump and Hegseth had been "the honor of a lifetime."

"I had the privilege of working with them to modernize and accelerate how the Army mans, trains, and equips the most lethal fighting force on the face of the earth," Driscoll said in a statement posted on X.
"We could not have made the progress we did without the support of Secretary Hegseth," he continued. "I am forever grateful to President Trump for the opportunity to once again serve my country."

title: EXCLUSIVE: FBI extraditions soar as Patel ramps up foreign outreach, vows 'no sanctuary'
summary: FBI Director Kash Patel says FBI extraditions of international fugitives to the United States are up 65%, with 157 executed amid a sweeping manhunt push.
story: Arizona murder suspect Varun Batchigari faces extradition from Germany after his arrest in the killing of girlfriend Julissa Salazar. Former DOJ prosecutor Jim Trusty analyzes the international legal hurdles in bringing the suspect back to face charges, while discussing Vice President JD Vance's warning about migrant welfare fraud.
FIRST ON FOX: FBI Director Kash Patel has dramatically expanded direct outreach to foreign partners in an effort to bring international fugitives back to the United States.

FBI data exclusively obtained by Fox News Digital shows Patel made 100 calls to international partners in his first 18 months, compared with nine by his predecessor during the final 18 months of the Biden administration.

Compared to the last 18 months of the Biden administration, extraditions were up 65%, and FTOCs (foreign transfer of custody), in which a fugitive or suspect is apprehended overseas and transferred into U.S. custody, are up 54%, the FBI said.
In that time, the FBI has executed 157 extraditions and 86 FTOCs.
FBI BRINGS BACK FUGITIVE ACCUSED IN $3.7B MEDICARE FRAUD SCHEME AFTER CAPTURE IN TURKEY

FBI Director Kash Patel touted the agency's facilitation of foreign transfers of custody and the uptick in extraditions of high-profile targets seeking to evade U.S. justice abroad. (Win McNamee/Getty Images/File)
"When I became FBI director, I made clear that we would relentlessly manhunt high‑value targets from overseas, and we’ve delivered," FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital.

"It’s a direct result of President [Donald] Trump’s relationships with foreign governments, which allow us to work in spaces where we were never permitted to before and Attorney General Todd Blanche’s leadership giving us the legal tools we need to return these subjects back to America to face charges.
"These targets are literally the worst of the worst, and we will give them no sanctuary."
MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING WIFE ON WEDDING NIGHT BROUGHT BACK TO US AFTER YEARS ON THE RUN IN MEXICO
Alexis Flores was previously a top 10 FBI fugitive, according to officials. He was arrested Wednesday in Honduras in the 2000 murder of a young girl in Philadelphia. (FBI and Google Maps)

On Monday, a Honduran citizen on the FBI's 10 Most Wanted Fugitives list was extradited to Philadelphia after 25 years on the run for the alleged rape and murder of a 5-year-old girl, Fox News exclusively reported.

Alexis Flores was arrested in February, and Honduran authorities agreed to extradite him to the U.S. The FBI said Flores had been removed from the fugitives list in March 2025 due to the prior Honduran government’s refusal to extradite him for his offenses, citing local laws limiting extradition.
EXCLUSIVE: ALLEGED $32M COVID-19 FRAUD FUGITIVE CAPTURED IN JAMAICA AND RETURNED TO US, FBI SAYS
FBI agents escort Zobaidul Amin after his transfer from Malaysia to the United States to face charges in an alleged international sextortion and child exploitation scheme. (Department of Justice)
Since June, the FBI has conducted more than 70 extraditions, Patel said at the time of Flores' extradition to the U.S.
In March, Zobaidul Amin, a Bangladeshi national, was extradited from Malaysia to the U.S. to face charges related to one of the most prolific online child exploitation schemes.

Prosecutors allege Amin posed as a teenager on Instagram and Snapchat and coerced hundreds of minor victims — some as young as 11 — into producing sexually explicit images and videos. Authorities said he then threatened to share those images with friends, family and classmates unless the victims sent more.

Another recent example is the case of Abdullah Anwar, 28, a Texas resident who was brought back from Qatar to face fraud charges. Anwar fled the U.S. for Pakistan but was arrested in Qatar before authorities there agreed to extradite him to Texas.
FBI WRAPS UP CYBERCRIME OPERATION TARGETING GLOBAL NETWORKS PREYING ON AMERICANS

The FBI has prioritized the extradition of suspects and fugitives abroad. From 2022 to 2025, former FBI Director Christopher Wray made 20 calls to foreign partners, including nine in his last 18 months during the Biden administration, the agency said.
Patel has made 100 calls in his first 18 months, a 400% increase over those made during Wray's four years and a 1,011% call increase over Wray's final 18 months with the Biden administration.
FBI agents stand on the tarmac as a plane arrives carrying Zobaidul Amin after his extradition from Malaysia to face federal charges in Alaska. (Department of Justice)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Typically, the FBI works with foreign authorities and governments to track and arrest suspects hiding in other countries. Once someone is arrested, the Justice Department will formally request that person be handed over to U.S. custody using existing international treaties.
Once the foreign government approves the handover, FBI agents travel abroad, take physical custody of the fugitive and fly them back to the U.S. for trial.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Steel Across America tour lands at Fenway Park ahead of 25th anniversary of 9/11
summary: The 21-foot World Trade Center steel beam drew emotional reactions at Fenway Park as fans shared deeply personal connections to the 9/11 attacks.
story: The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America tour landed at Fenway Park this week ahead of the 25th anniversary of 9/11. (Tunnel to Towers Foundation)
The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America tour landed at Boston's Fenway Park Wednesday night, giving Red Sox fans a chance to see a preserved section of the World Trade Center.
The 21-foot steel beam from the South Tower of the World Trade Center has been on a tour across America since May, and it is scheduled to finish its journey in New York City just after Sept. 11.
"It brings up a lot of memories, and, honestly, reading that and talking to the firemen over there, it can give me chills. It gives me chills," Fenway vendor David Littlefield said of the display.
WHERE TUNNEL TO TOWERS' STEEL ACROSS AMERICA TOUR WILL STOP AHEAD OF 9/11
The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America tour landed in Fenway Park on Thursday.  (Steel Across America)
"It was gut-wrenching, heartbreaking," he said, adding that his wife lost a roommate in the attacks.
"It hits home. I worked for American Airlines for 30 years, and I … worked Flight 11 and Flight 77 many times," another woman at the game said.
I LOST MY WIFE ON 9/11. PLEASE LET THIS 25TH ANNIVERSARY BELONG TO THE FAMILIES
The display is now being featured at the Massachusetts Fallen Heroes Memorial on Thursday.
A banner above the entrance to Fenway Park.  (Steel Across America)

The 16,900-pound beam will then head to the nation's capital, where it will be featured at a private event on Friday. It will then head to New York City for another private event in Brooklyn on Sept. 11, before a final appearance at the New York Giants vs. Dallas Cowboys game at MetLife Stadium Sept. 13.
NFL TO COMMEMORATE 25TH ANNIVERSARY OF 9/11 TERRORIST ATTACKS ACROSS ALL ITS STADIUMS AND EVEN IN AUSTRALIA

The beam visited the U.S. Military Academy at West Point on Monday, where the superintendent, Lt. Gen. James B. Bartholomees III, said the piece of steel connects the courage shown by first responders on 9/11 with the Americans who answered the call to serve in the years that followed.

"As we approach the 25th anniversary of 9/11, this piece of steel reminds us of the courage of first responders like Stephen Siller and the countless Americans who answered the call in the years that followed, including generations of West Point graduates," Bartholomees said. "Today, young men and women continue that legacy of service, guided by duty, honor country."

Army personnel and Frank Siller view a steel beam recovered from the World Trade Center's South Tower during its stop at West Point. (Jason Thiele Fotografik Memories/Courtesy Tunnel to Towers Foundation)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The ceremony brought together cadets, faculty, staff and guests and opened with a color guard and pipe and drum procession by members of the NYPD, FDNY and Port Authority Police Department. The program also included the national anthem, an invocation and blessing of the steel and a moment of reflection accompanied by "Amazing Grace."
Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.

title: DOJ charges ICE officer with lying to investigators following Minneapolis shooting of Venezuelan man
summary: ICE agent Christian Castro faces federal false statements charges tied to the shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis during an immigration crackdown.
story: Fox News correspondent Christina Coleman reports from Dallas on a federal judge blocking attempts by Minnesota to extradite ICE agent Christian Castro from Texas. Castro faces charges stemming from the January shooting of a Venezuelan migrant during Operation Metro Surge in Minneapolis, while Texas Gov. Greg Abbott investigates whether the officer legally qualifies as a fugitive.

Federal prosecutors have charged a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer with lying to investigators about the events surrounding the shooting of a Venezuelan man in Minneapolis earlier this year, Fox News Digital has learned.

The Department of Justice has charged ICE agent Christian Castro with making false statements connected to the Jan. 14 shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, who was shot in the leg. He was indicted by a federal grand jury in Minnesota on Wednesday, a source familiar with the charges said.

Castro is accused of opening fire through the front door of a Minneapolis home, hitting Sosa-Celis, and then lying about the events before the shooting. The incident came amid the Trump administration's crackdown on illegal immigration in Minnesota.
ICE OFFICER CHARGED IN MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING RELEASED IN TEXAS AFTER JUDGE DECLINES TO INTERVENE

Left: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer Christian Castro gets into a car surrounded by news reporters moments after being released from the Carrizalez-Rucker Cameron County Detention Center in Brownsville, Texas on Aug. 27. Federal prosecutors have charged with lying about the Jan. 14 shooting of a Venezuelan man in Minneapolis. (Left: AP Photo/Michael Gonzalez; Right: Cameron County Sheriff's Office)
What followed was at least one night of unrest in Minneapolis.
The charges came after Castro was released from a Texas jail last week, following Texas Gov. Greg Abbott's refusal to sign an extradition warrant to hand him over to Minnesota authorities.

Under Texas law and barring extradition, Castro must be released after 90 days of detention. Last month, Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison filed an unsuccessful request for a temporary restraining order in an effort to block Castro’s release or to order his return to Minnesota, The Associated Press reported.
ABBOTT TAUNTS FAR-LEFT AG WITH FIERY WARNING OVER ICE EXTRADITION FIGHT: 'SUCH BAD LAWYERS'

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott (left) and Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison (right) battled on X over whether an ICE agent involved in a recent shooting in Minneapolis should be extradited back to Minnesota. (Getty Images)
Castro is charged separately in that state with assault and false reporting of a crime related to the same shooting.
Federal authorities initially accused Sosa-Celis and another man of beating an officer with a broom handle and a snow shovel during a confrontation.
ICE SAYS OFFICER SHOT AND KILLED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT WHO TRIED TO RAM HIM WITH CAR IN HOUSTON
However, the charges were dropped after video evidence showed the officers may have lied about the encounter, prompting an investigation.
On Wednesday, ProPublica reported that federal prosecutors were barred by officials in Washington from pursuing civil rights charges against Castro.

Fox News Digital has reached out to ICE, the Department of Homeland Security and the Justice Department for comment.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Israeli medics train US synagogues how to respond to attacks, as high holidays approach
summary: Magen David Adom and Community Security Service train synagogue volunteers in mass casualty response as antisemitism fears grow before Rosh Hashanah.
story: Aryeh Myers is a senior paramedic and International Affairs representative for Magen David Adom, Israel's emergency medical service. He has held trainings for volunteers in the U.S. seeking to learn how to respond after a terror attack.
Jewish communities across the U.S. are ramping up their security measures and emergency preparation ahead of Rosh Hashanah and other High Holidays.

Israel's emergency medical service, Magen David Adom, partnered with the U.S.-based Community Security Service to hold trainings for security volunteers at synagogues across the country. Senior paramedic Aryeh Myers told Fox News Digital that community members remain deeply concerned about a rise in antisemitism.
"There is this heightened sense of concern, of worry that these attacks are now a question of when rather than if," Myers said in an interview.
MARYLAND SYNAGOGUE SUES COUNTY OVER LAW RESTRICTING CONCEALED CARRY NEAR HOUSES OF WORSHIP
Israeli senior paramedic Aryeh Myers trains volunteers on the First 7 Minutes course New York. (Community Security Service)

Myers has held First 7 Minutes trainings in the U.S. and elsewhere with Jewish, Christian and non-religious groups, teaching volunteers how to respond in the minutes after an attack has occurred and before first responders have arrived.
His trainings focus on first aid, how to communicate most effectively with first responders and how best to assist them once they do arrive.
MAN CHARGED WITH ASSAULT, HATE CRIMES AFTER ALLEGEDLY DISRUPTING SHABBAT SERVICES AT NYC SYNAGOGUE
Volunteers receive training on how to respond after a mass-casualty attack. (Community Security Service)
"Our expertise is in response to mass casualty events.... We respond on the national level to everything from delivering babies, to terror attacks to war situations," Myers said.

"The advantage that Magen David Adom brings is unfortunately having that level of experience, that we have seen multiple mass casualty attacks and multi-casualty attacks and have learned from those," he added.
ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE ESCALATES AS DEADLY WEAPON ATTACKS SURGE IN 2025: REPORT
Jewish communities across the globe have faced increasing levels of antisemitism in the years since the October 7 terror attacks in Israel.
Many U.S. universities became hotbeds for anti-Israel and antisemitic attacks amid Israel's war against Hamas in Gaza.
JEWISH EDUCATORS FACE RAMPANT ANTISEMITISM IN TEACHERS UNIONS, NEW REPORT FINDS
A new report from the Anti-Defamation League (ADL) found that Jewish teachers have also faced rampant antisemitism from teachers unions.
The organization surveyed 307 Jewish members of teachers unions, many of whom admitted to censoring themselves and being disappointed with how unions handled concerns about antisemitism.
The Anti-Defamation League warns in a new report that antisemitism is not only found at on-campus protests, but also in classrooms. (Drazen Zigic/iStock/Getty Images Plus)
BACK TO SCHOOL SHOULD NOT MEAN BACK TO FEAR FOR JEWISH STUDENTS

"What we found is not the work of a few bad actors. It is a structural and cultural failure," ADL CEO Jonathan Greenblatt said in a statement. "Jewish educators deserve to feel safe and protected in their union spaces. And instead of that, they are self-censoring and fearing backlash for raising concerns."

Sydney Altfield, CEO of Teach Coalition, an organization that advocates for Jewish schools, said the report was particularly concerning because teachers unions were meant to represent and protect all educators.
THE BRAVEST JEWS IN AMERICA ARE 15 YEARS OLD — AND THEY’RE GOING BACK TO SCHOOL
"What strikes me is that these unions are supposed to be homes for everyone, and [they're] not being that," Altfield told Fox News Digital.

One of the key findings of the report was the high rate at which Jewish educators were self-censoring out of fear of retaliation. According to the ADL, 70% of respondents "somewhat or strongly agreed" that bringing up concerns about how Jews were treated in union spaces "could lead to reputational or professional consequences."
Fox News' Rachel Wolf contributed to this report.
Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.

title: Trump negotiators Witkoff, Kushner arrive in Moscow as US pushes for end to Russia-Ukraine war
summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have landed in Moscow for peace talks before heading to Kyiv, as Trump says there may be a good chance for a deal.
story: During an open to the press event in the White House's Oval Office on Friday, Sept. 4, 2026, President Donald Trump explains his decision to send special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv. Credit: Reuters.

U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and President Donald Trump's son-in-law and adviser, Jared Kushner, are visiting Moscow and Kyiv over the weekend in an effort to end the war between Russia and Ukraine, President Donald Trump said Friday.

"We have an idea for peace," Trump told reporters on Friday. "I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, two great negotiators. They've done a great job, and we sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done. And there may be a good chance that we'll do it," he said.
Ukrainian President Volodomyr Zelenskyy confirmed the news in a post on X.

"Today, it has been clearly established that U.S. envoys will be in Ukraine and Russia in the coming days. We have the details from the U.S. President’s team. We discussed today that Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will visit Moscow and then Kyiv on Sunday. We are preparing for the visit," Zelenskyy wrote.
TRUMP ANNOUNCES SURPRISE THREE-DAY CEASEFIRE IN RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR

Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev greets U.S. special representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff upon their arrival at Vnukovo International Airport in Moscow, Russia, Sept. 5, 2026. (Reuters)
The pair will visit Russia first on Saturday and, according to Russian state-affiliated media outlet Tass, have already landed in Moscow.
They will then move on to Kyiv on Sunday, Zelenskyy confirmed. Zelenskyy also said that Ukraine will work to keep Russian airspace safe during the Americans’ visit.
CIA DIRECTOR JOHN RATCLIFFE MET WITH RUSSIAN INTELLIGENCE OFFICIALS IN VISIT TO MOSCOW, KREMLIN SAYS

Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev walks with U.S. special representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff upon their arrival at Vnukovo International Airport in Moscow, Russia, Sept. 5, 2026. (Reuters)

"Just as we did during previous diplomatic visits by the American side, we will ensure the normal functioning of Russian airspace so that the negotiators can arrive safely. We are looking out for them, not for Russia. There will be no air strikes from our side, and Russia must do the same, ensuring there are no air strikes from its side for the time needed to hold these talks and handle the logistical matters related to this American visit," he wrote on X.
ZELENSKYY CONGRATULATES TRUMP ON TURNING 80 IN BIRTHDAY CALL, VOWS MORE UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AT G7 ON TUESDAY

"Our goal is to make the visit and the talks with the U.S. side as constructive and substantive as possible. We need to look for real options for how to move this war toward an end. We will see what proposals Steve and Jared bring and what they are told in Moscow in response," the Ukrainain president concluded.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky speaks at a press conference after meetings with the heads of the EU and Ireland, following a formal ceremony to mark the launch of Ireland's eighth EU presidency, at Dublin Castle in Dublin on July 1, 2026. (Paul Faith / AFP via Getty Images)
Zelenskyy’s Friday message came the same day that a Russian drone strike targeted the Security Service of Ukraine’s headquarters in Ukraine, Zelenskyy wrote in a public message on the app Telegram.
RUSSIA LAUNCHES BALLISTIC MISSILE ATTACK ON KYIV HOURS AFTER ZELENSKYY WARNS OF MAJOR STRIKE
Zelenskyy alleged the strike directly targeted the head of the Security Service's office.

He also wrote that he was directing the head, Oleksandr Poklad, to prepare a retaliatory strike. "I gave Poklad the task of adequately, noticeably and, if possible, mirroring the Russians' response to this attack, when everything is prepared. Our military will support this response. Glory to Ukraine!" he wrote.
PUTIN UNLEASHES NEW FURY ON UKRAINE AS REPORT EXPOSES FEAR HANGING OVER WAR’S END
At least nine people were injured in the explosion, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko also wrote on Telegram.

A man looks on as smoke rises over a warehouse, which was hit by a Russian drone strike, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Kyiv region, Ukraine, Aug. 27, 2026. (REUTERS/Valentyn Ogirenko/File Photo)
The visit also comes just one day after German officials formally accused Russia of attempting an explosive drone attack on a major airport in Germany.
RUSSIA’S STRIKES NEAR MOLDOVA RAISE ALARM OVER PUTIN’S PLANS FOR EUROPE’S EASTERN FLANK

"The attack on the aircraft in Leipzig was concrete; it could have triggered a catastrophe had it succeeded. The attacker was, at most, covert, but even here there is now certainty: The German government has named Russia as the mastermind. Patterns of attack, police investigations, and intelligence findings prove Russian responsibility for the drone attack," Stefan Kornelius, a spokesperson for the German federal government, wrote Friday.

title: Russia's shadow war is putting Europe on edge as Germany confronts a growing threat
summary: Germany accused Russia of a drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport and now pushes Baltic Sea allies to form a rapid-response hybrid warfare task force.
story: Jennifer Griffin reports on Russia's shadow fleet launching a drone campaign across Europe to surveil military sites and test NATO's air defenses. The International Institute for Strategic Studies report reveals 144 suspected drones near sensitive sites in Germany, France, and the UK.

Germany is pushing European partners to create a rapid-response task force in the Baltic Sea region as Berlin confronts what it says is an escalating campaign of Russian hybrid warfare, including an attempted explosives-laden drone attack on one of the country's most important cargo airports.

The initiative, proposed by German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt following an Aug. 28 meeting in Flensburg, is intended to allow Baltic Sea countries to rapidly exchange information and coordinate responses to hybrid threats ranging from drones and sabotage to cyberattacks, disinformation and attacks on critical infrastructure.
"We want to turn this shared threat environment into a shared security environment," Dobrindt said, warning that hybrid threats were becoming more frequent and sophisticated.
The proposal has taken on new urgency after Germany formally accused Russia this week of responsibility for an attempted Aug. 4 attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport involving a drone carrying explosives.
EXPLOSIVE DRONE FORCES SHUTDOWN AT MAJOR GERMAN AIRPORT SERVING NATO, UKRAINE FLIGHTS

A drone carrying explosives was found at Germany's Leipzig/Halle Airport on Tuesday night next to a Ukrainian plane, with officials warning the incident represented "a new quality of danger." (Hendrik Schmidt/DPA via AP)

German officials said police findings, intelligence information and the methods used in the attack led Berlin to conclude Russia was responsible. The government said aspects of the drone, explosives and detonation technology were consistent with methods seen in previous Russian hybrid operations and in Moscow's war against Ukraine.

Germany has not publicly released much of the underlying evidence, saying details including information about suspected perpetrators, travel routes, surveillance footage and DNA evidence are being withheld to protect the investigation.
Latvia characterized the Leipzig attack in even stronger terms.

"The attack in Leipzig confirms once again that Russia poses a direct threat to the security of all of Europe. This was not merely a hybrid attack, but state-sponsored terrorism on German soil," Latvian Foreign Minister Baiba Braže said in a statement published by Latvia's Foreign Ministry.
Braže also called for continued efforts to strengthen Ukraine's defense capabilities and for additional sanctions aimed at limiting Russia's ability to produce missiles, drones and other weapons.
US INTEL WARNS RUSSIA COULD LAUNCH LIMITED ATTACK ON NATO ALLY IN EFFORT TO FRAGMENT ORGANIZATION: REPORT

Russia's ambassador to Germany, Sergei Nechayev, attends an event in Berlin in May. Germany summoned Nechayev after accusing Moscow of carrying out the failed drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport. (Christoph Soeder/Picture Alliance via Getty Images, File)
Retired Air Force Lt. Gen. Richard Newton told Fox News Digital that the episode reflects what he described as a widening pattern of hostile activity.

"We are clearly seeing an escalation in the scope and intensity of Russian gray-zone hostile actions across Europe," Newton said. "Russia has long used a variety of non-military, covert, and hybrid tactics – cyberattacks, information operations, sabotage, other covert means – to create disruption while staying just below the threshold of open conflict with NATO."
Newton called Germany's attribution of the Leipzig plot "particularly serious," saying it "demonstrates how dangerous these operations are becoming."

Germany responded by announcing the closure of Russia's consulate general in Bonn and ending the arrangement governing the Russian House cultural center in Berlin. Berlin also said it would tighten entry controls for Russian nationals and increase pressure on Russia's so-called shadow fleet.
Russia has denied responsibility for the Leipzig incident, calling Germany's accusations "entirely fabricated" and accusing Berlin of escalating tensions, according to Reuters.
The heightened concern comes as German police separately investigate a cluster of suspected sabotage incidents targeting the country's electricity infrastructure this week.
REPORT WARNS RUSSIA USING SHADOW FLEET TO PROBE NATO DRONE DEFENSES

Polish soldiers stand watch near the Belarus border, where officials say migration pressure has evolved into a form of hybrid warfare targeting NATO’s eastern flank. May 16th, 2026. (Efrat Lachter/Fox News Digital)
Authorities were investigating a suspicious device found near a substation in Dormagen, North Rhine-Westphalia, on Friday, following incidents in Bergheim and Brandenburg.
In Bergheim, deliberate interference temporarily forced lignite-fired generating units representing about 4,200 megawatts of capacity offline, though no broader blackout occurred.
German authorities have not publicly connected those power-grid incidents to Russia, a distinction Newton said was important.
"We need to be careful when attributing these hostile acts and ensure we have indisputable intelligence information that clearly leads to the source of these belligerent actions," Newton said.
"The incidents involving Germany’s power infrastructure are still under investigation and have not been publicly attributed to Russia, or any other source for that matter," he added.
The German government nevertheless said Friday that the country faces a persistent hybrid threat.
"Germany is not at war, but it is a daily target of hybrid warfare," the government said, citing attacks on communications systems, disinformation and arson targeting the defense industry.
EUROPE BANKROLLS PUTIN'S WAR MACHINE EVEN AS NATO RACES TO BOLSTER DEFENSES
NATO Chiefs of Defense hold a hybrid meeting with screens showing allied leaders joining remotely, Aug. 20 2025. (NATO)

Retired Gen. Philip Breedlove, former NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe, told Fox News Digital that Moscow has increasingly sought to pressure Western countries while avoiding conventional conflict.

"We do know that Russia is trying to fight the Western world below the line of kinetic conflict and their methods are getting ever bolder, whether through cyber operations, sabotage, drones and other forms of pressure across Europe," Breedlove said. "We’re even becoming aware of things they are doing inside the United States."
Breedlove said Russian President Vladimir Putin has long sought to exploit divisions within NATO, "especially between the United States and Europe."
"The Western world has got to step up to counter the Russian threat," he said.

The Baltic initiative comes amid broader efforts by NATO and regional governments to protect an area increasingly associated with threats to undersea cables, pipelines, shipping and other critical infrastructure.
NATO already operates Baltic Sentry, an enhanced vigilance activity launched in 2025 to strengthen protection of critical undersea infrastructure in the Baltic Sea.

In February, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland and Sweden agreed to accelerate the acquisition and integration of new technologies for Baltic naval operations. NATO said that initiative built on testing involving roughly 70 aerial and maritime drones in 2025.
Breedlove said Germany's proposed task force could help bridge intelligence, law-enforcement and military responses among regional partners.

"Germany’s Baltic initiative makes sense," he said. "The value is also for partner countries to share information faster, connect the intelligence, law-enforcement and military pieces, and make decisions before Russia can take advantage of confusion or delay."
Newton similarly said the task force could complement NATO's existing military activity by improving governments' ability to rapidly share intelligence and coordinate security responses.
Breedlove warned that Moscow would continue searching for opportunities to exploit uncertainty.

BALTIC SEA (June 5, 2025) The Blue Ridge-class command and control ship USS Mount Whitney (LCC 20) participates in exercise Baltic Operations 2025 (BALTOPS 25) as ships sail in formation through the Baltic Sea, June 5, 2025. BALTOPS 25, the premiere maritime-focused exercise in the Baltic Region, provides a unique training opportunity to strengthen combined response capabilities critical to preserving freedom of navigation and security in the Baltic Sea. (U.S. Navy Courtesy Photo)

"Without question, the Russians will keep looking for places where they can create uncertainty and hesitation," he said. "We need to get better at recognizing their actions with speed – and responding forcefully with the strength of our allies."

Fox News Digital reached out to the German Embassy in Washington, D.C., and the Russian Embassy in Washington, D.C., for comment but did not receive responses by publication time.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: From cockroach milk to stepping on snakes, Ig Nobel awards celebrates science at its oddest
summary: Cockroach milk, kissing evolution and the underwear soil test were among the unusual real studies honored at the Ig Nobel ceremony in Zurich.
story: An Arkansas high school football player discovered a cottonmouth snake inside his helmet after completing a practice. Animal control was able to remove the two-foot reptile from the padding after he wore the equipment during practice.

A motley crew of scientists was honored this week for its unusual contributions, which included studying cockroach milk, the evolutionary history of kissing and testing soil health by using underwear.
The satirical Ig Nobel ceremony, which honors unusual but real studies, took place in Zurich Thursday and was presented by the digital magazine, the Annals of Improbable Research.
The awards, which were founded in 1991, took place outside the U.S. for the first time this year over the concern that the honorees wouldn’t be able to get a visa.

Other winners included researchers who found upper-class people were more likely to engage in unethical behavior, such as stealing candy from a baby, a study on proper nose blowing and gently stepping on snakes to see what provokes them into biting people.
WASHINGTON HOMEOWNER HEARS MYSTERIOUS BANGING CALLS 911 BEFORE POLICE FIND GROWLING BOBCAT AT TOP OF STAIRS

Soil Science Prize winners Pia Viviani, right, and Atlant Bieri, left, stand on stage during the Ig Nobel Prize ceremony at the Zurich Convention Center in Zurich, Switzerland, Thursday. (Claudio Thoma/Keystone via AP)

"The general pattern seems to be that, with wealth and rising power, you become less engaged with the needs of others and less burdened by the needs of social relationships," Dr. Paul Piff, a social psychologist at the University of California, Irvine said, according to the Guardian.
"Taking candy from children might be the least of our worries, but it’s emblematic of the tendency to prioritize one’s own needs over those of others."

The final four honorees included those studying the power of having mutual enemies, attempts at a splash-free urinal, using dead mosquitos for 3D printing and research that found parents love the smell of their newborn babies but not teenage children.

In case you’re wondering, the team studying the history of kissing has defined it as "a non-agonistic interaction involving directed, intraspecific, oral-oral contact with some movement of the lips/mouthparts and no food transfer." Romantic.

From left, Nobel Prize winners Esther Duflo, Abhijit Banerjee, Michel Mayor and Tim Hunt look at underwear handed over by the Soil Science Award winners during the Ig Nobel Prize ceremony at the Zurich Convention Center in Zurich, Switzerland, Thursday. (Claudio Thoma/Keystone via AP)
COUPLE PUBLICLY CANED AFTER ALLEGED TIKTOK KISS SPARKS OUTRAGE IN INDONESIA

"Next time you kiss someone, you can think, 'This is a 21.5 million-year-old tradition that I'm honoring here," evolutionary biologist Matilda Brindle of the University of Oxford said, according to NPR. "It's not just a modern human behavior. It's really ancestral.' And to us, that suggests that it probably has quite a useful evolutionary function."
Brindle said her team believes that Neanderthals not only kissed each other. They may have also kissed early humans.
CAVE DISCOVERY PUSHES BACK EVIDENCE OF HUMAN ANCESTORS USING FIRE TO 1.79M YEARS AGO
The winners of the Ig Nobel Prize pose for a group picture during the ceremony at the Zurich Convention Center in Zurich, Switzerland, Thursday. (Claudio Thoma/Keystone via AP)
All the honorees receive a trophy that looks like a cross between a mushroom and a human foot while the audience throws paper airplanes at them.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The Ig Nobel has no relation to the actual Nobel Prize, which will announce its honorees in October.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Trapped Nepal workers pulled alive from tunnel 9 days after deadly flooding, raising hope for more rescues
summary: Two workers were pulled alive from a Nepal hydropower tunnel nine days after catastrophic floods, and one rescued man says more people are trapped inside.
story: On Friday morning, searchers heard men's voices, which prompted an all-out rescue mission with the help of the Nepal Army. (Credit: Nepali Army via Storyful)
Rescue teams in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a hydropower tunnel nine days after catastrophic floods swept through the country, leaving more than 1,000 people dead and thousands more missing.

Nepalese lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane told The Associated Press that searchers first heard men's voices in the tunnel on Friday morning. Images distributed by the Nepal Army showed a rescuer carrying one of the workers on his back while soldiers on either side helped.

The breakthrough has raised hopes that the dozens of others believed to be trapped will be rescued. One of the rescued men said more people are alive inside the tunnel, according to Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, who said the search is ongoing.
SON REALIZES MISSING AMERICAN DAD WAS IN PATH OF NEPAL DISASTER AFTER WATCHING VIRAL VIDEO
Soldiers rescue a worker alive from a tunnel during an ongoing operation at the Trishuli-3A hydropower project in Nepal's Rasuwa district on Sept. 4, 2026. (Nepal Army via AP)
"I can’t explain what we are feeling at the moment. We are just grateful to God," Amir Maharjan, the brother of one of those rescued, told the AP.
Both men were flown to a hospital in Kathmandu, and one of them was in critical condition, the AP reported, citing a statement from the prime minister's office.
Officials identified them as a mechanical foreman and a mechanical supervisor at the Trishuli 3A plant.
On Sept. 4, 2026, a rescuer carried one of the workers who was trapped for days in the tunnel at the Trishuli-3A hydropower project. Soldiers flank him on either side. (Nepal Army via AP)
TERRIFYING VIDEO CAPTURES PEOPLE FLEEING INCOMING MUDSLIDE AT NEPAL-CHINA BORDER
The AP reported that about 115 people are believed to remain trapped in the Trishuli 3A tunnel alone, citing the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal.
In total, authorities say there are about 900 workers missing from 12 hydropower plants in Nepal, with about 500 of them believed to be trapped in tunnels.
Nepal’s Communication Minister Bikram Timilsina wrote on his Facebook page that officials "are waiting for the rescue of more and more people."
"A heartfelt thank you to everyone who worked tirelessly day and night to rescue two people alive!" Timilsina added.
One of the workers, covered in mud, is lifted out of the tunnel by rescue teams on Sept. 4, 2026. (Nepal Army via AP)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The AP reported that at least 1,287 people have been killed and more than 5,000 remain missing after the Aug. 26 floods, which scientists believe were likely triggered by a glacier collapse.
China said on Wednesday that on the Tibet side of the border, 21 people were killed and 541 are missing.
Nepal's disaster agency chief told Reuters on Friday that the flooding has likely caused at least 387.5 billion Nepalese rupees (about $2.5 billion) in damage to infrastructure and property.
The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.
James Cirrone is a writer on the Breaking/Trending News team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to james.cirrone@fox.com.

title: US adversary turns up the heat on America’s AI lead with an underestimated edge
summary: China's "East Data, West Computing" initiative is rapidly expanding AI infrastructure, but a major chip constraint complicates Beijing's push.
story: China expert Gordon Chang discusses why he believes Beijing is looking to exploit US opposition to new data centers as China works to narrow America’s lead in AI infrastructure.

China is racing to build the data centers and energy infrastructure needed to power artificial intelligence, raising concerns that Beijing’s ability to rapidly construct massive projects could help it get closer to America’s commanding lead in the physical infrastructure underpinning the AI race.

The U.S. remains far ahead in sheer numbers. The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence’s 2026 AI Index, using Cloudscene data, counted 5,427 U.S. data centers in 2025 compared with 449 in China. Stanford cautioned that the count does not account for differences in facility size, computing capacity or utilization.
But China is moving quickly.
AMERICA IS FIGHTING YESTERDAY’S AI WAR. TOMORROW’S WAR IS ON THE WAY
People visit the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai, China, July 18, 2026. (Go Nakamura/Reuters)
"We know that China is far behind, but we also know that they are moving at great speed," China expert Gordon Chang told Fox News Digital.

Chang argued that Beijing understands the U.S. advantage will be difficult to erase if America continues building at the same pace and said growing opposition to data-center development could slow that expansion.
President Donald Trump made a similar argument this week, warning communities fighting new projects that China stands to benefit.

"China could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Actually, they can’t believe it is happening!" Trump also argued that communities embracing data centers would gain jobs and tax revenues.
Vice President JD Vance sharpened that warning Thursday, telling FOX Business there was "a very good chance" the U.S. could lose the AI race to China if Democrats regain control of Congress.

Vance said the broader problem is America’s ability to build enough power to support data centers and other major infrastructure. "We cannot be a country that says we’re not going to build more power," Vance said, arguing that the administration is trying to make it easier to construct power plants alongside data centers while protecting residential ratepayers from higher electricity costs.
AI BOOM: DEMAND FOR DATA CENTERS DRIVES INNOVATION BY ENERGY, TECH INDUSTRIES TO PRODUCE NEW POWER SOURCES

He also pointed to the widening U.S.-China electricity gap, saying China now generates roughly three times as much power as the United States. "We’ve got to build more power plants. We’ve got to make the regulatory state easier to work with."
Asked about China’s rapid infrastructure expansion, the Chinese Embassy in Washington rejected the premise that AI should primarily be viewed as a geopolitical contest.
"AI should not be owned by major countries, still less dominated by contests and rivalry," Embassy spokesperson Liu Chang told Fox News Digital.

Liu pointed to China’s 2025 Global AI Governance Action Plan, which calls for accelerating construction of clean power, next-generation networks, computing capacity and data centers. He said China advocates cooperation with the U.S. and wants AI development to benefit both countries and the broader international community.
Behind that diplomatic message, Beijing is undertaking a massive geographic reorganization of its computing infrastructure.

Under China’s "East Data, West Computing" initiative, Beijing is directing more computing capacity toward western regions where land is available and wind and solar resources can help reduce energy costs.

Five of China’s eight national computing hubs are located in western China, according to a June 25 report from the government-backed Digital China initiative. More than 30 data centers were under construction within a three-kilometer area in Horinger, Inner Mongolia, while intensive construction was also underway in Zhongwei, Ningxia.
Huawei Technology Co.'s new data center is seen under construction in Guian New Zone, in southwestern China's Guizhou province May 14, 2019. Picture taken May 14, 2019. (Reuters)
That buildout caught the attention of members of the bipartisan US-China Economic and Security Review Commission during a recent fact-finding trip to China.

"I left with an intense belief that the Chinese see this as the frontier in terms of competition," Commission Vice Chairman Mike Kuiken told Fox News Digital, describing AI as increasingly intertwined with robotics, biotechnology, advanced materials and manufacturing.
Kuiken said China has one significant advantage when it comes to constructing the infrastructure needed to support that technology.
"The Chinese, because they write the rules as they go, and the rule of law largely does not exist, are able to just move faster in terms of building things," he said.
But Kuiken also identified a major Chinese weakness: access to the most advanced chips.

"The constraints that are real though, the Chinese do not have the ability to procure advanced chips," he said, while describing Beijing’s ability to rapidly construct coal plants and other infrastructure as "quite incredible."
THE WAR ON DATA CENTERS JEOPARDIZES OUR ECONOMY AND NATIONAL SECURITY
The AI boom is accelerating demand for data centers across Texas as companies seek more space, power and infrastructure to support increasingly intensive computing needs. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images)

The U.S. retains major advantages beyond its data-center lead. The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence’s 2026 AI Index found that America produced 59 notable AI models in 2025 compared with 35 from China, and U.S. private AI investment reached $285.9 billion, compared with $12.4 billion in China. Stanford cautioned that private investment figures understate Beijing’s overall spending because of Chinese government-backed funds.
At the same time, Chinese models have rapidly narrowed the performance gap. Stanford’s 2026 AI Index found that as of March 2026, the top U.S. model led the top Chinese model by just 2.7%.

Chang also alleged that Beijing is seeking to exploit American opposition to data centers and claimed China-linked networks have helped support protests against projects in the US. "These protests are not entirely organic," Chang told Fox News Digital.

Kuiken was cautious about portraying those local disputes as part of a broader anti-China fight, saying genuine U.S. opposition to data-center projects has also emerged over concerns including electricity costs, water use, noise and land development.

"We are building things in the U.S. faster than we have in a long time," he said, adding that policymakers are working through infrastructure constraints. "Usually there are local issues that are driving those things."
The emerging competition, therefore, is not simply over who develops the smartest AI model.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Robots fight during an MMA-style performance at Engine AI booth at the 2026 World Robot Conference, in Beijing, China, August 19, 2026. (Maxim Shemetov/Reuters)
It is increasingly a race over who can build the electricity, data centers, chips and networks needed to run those models at enormous scale — and how quickly they can build them.

She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition.
