Clarkson, of course, would transform from powerhouse singer to just plain powerhouse. She has scored a trio of No. 1 hits on the Billboard Hot 100 and won three Grammy Awards, with 14 other nominations under her belt. She became a coach on “The Voice” and just wrapped up her seven-year run as host of “The Kelly Clarkson Show,” which netted her multiple Daytime Emmy Awards for outstanding host and talk show.

All of those accomplishments and accolades were ahead of Clarkson, though, when she stopped by TODAY on Sept. 6, 2002, just two days after her “American Idol” win. It was a whirlwind time for her as the victory was quickly followed by a massive press tour.
“I just walked off a plane, so, yeah, I’m a little exhausted. But it’s cool. It’s cool. I love it,” the then-20-year-old told Katie Couric.
“I’ve done a little bit of everything,” she said about the previous 48 hours, alluding to all of the appearance she had made and noting how little she had slept.
Kelly Clarkson Understood the Impact of Her First Song
After she was announced as the winner, Clarkson sang “A Moment Like This,” which would become her first single — and first No. 1 hit. What was going through her mind as she sang?
“I was trying not to think of the words,” she said, laughing while Couric said the lyrics were “very relevant” to what Clarkson was experiencing at that point.
Kelly Clarkson Was in Awe That She Won
Clarkson was gobsmacked by the enormous odds she overcame to win the contest, even as she performed “A Moment Like This.”
“I guess I was thinking, there’s so many talented people out there, I can’t believe. Who would’ve thunk it, you know? Walking in, out of 10,000 people, I don’t know,” she said.
Kelly Clarkson Had Endured Plenty
Though only 20 at the time, Clarkson had already held many jobs while pursuing her dream as a singer.
“I’ve done everything,” she said, while first saying she had worked as a waitress before Couric asked her what else she had done.

“Oh, I’ve worked for the zoo,” she continued. “I’ve worked for bookstores. I’ve been a telemarketer. I’ve done door-to-door sales. You name it. You know, because I’m a performer. You never want that job. You know, you always want to do singing, so you’re never satisfied.”

title: Taylor Frankie Paul Says She Got Engaged on ‘Bachelorette’ Season That Never Aired
summary: Taylor Frankie Paul revealed that she got engaged while filming her season of “The Bachelorette,” which was pulled from the air just days before premiere.
story: Taylor Frankie Paul revealed that she got engaged while filming her season of “The Bachelorette,” which was pulled from the air just days before premiere.

Paul discussed the drama surrounding her shelved “Bachelorette” season in the upcoming Season 5 of “The Secret Lives of Mormon Lives,” as seen in a clip from the show shared by the Hulu podcast “Get Real” on Sept. 3.
The clip began with Paul appearing to deny to castmates Jessi Draper, Mayci Neeley and Mikayla Matthews that she was intimate with anyone in one of the fantasy suites on “The Bachelorette.”

Draper mentioned “The Bachelorette” suitor whom Paul reportedly chose, Doug Mason, without saying his name. She asked Paul if she ever thought Mason “looks like Dakota,” in reference to Paul’s ex-boyfriend, Dakota Mortensen, with whom Paul shares a son.
“I didn’t start thinking that until people said it around me,” Paul said.
“They have the same initials,” Draper responded. “They’re both from Idaho. It’s so weird.”
Paul then left her “Mormon Wives” castmates stunned when she revealed how her experience filming “The Bachelorette” ended.
“And yes, he did get down on one knee and proposed, which I was shocked,” she said.
Paul said she accepted the proposal.
“And then I come home,” she said.
She said she returned to Utah and began texting Mortensen.
“I don’t know how it led to it, but he came over,” Paul said.
Paul’s season of “The Bachelorette” was canceled in March after TMZ published a video reportedly from an altercation between Paul and Mortensen in 2023 that led to her arrest.
Paul later pled guilty in abeyance to aggravated assault, court records obtained by NBC News show.

The former couple was also involved in a domestic violence investigation earlier this year stemming from several alleged incidents from 2024 to 2026, police confirmed to NBC News. Reps for Mortensen and Paul declined to comment at the time. In April, the Salt Lake County District Attorney’s Office said neither Paul nor Mortensen would face new charges.
Filming for Season 5 of “Mormon Wives” was paused amid the investigation but picked back up around late April.
“Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” will return for Season 5 on Sept. 10.

title: Alix Earle Breaks Silence on Alex Cooper Feud. Everything She Said, Including a Full Text She Almost Sent Cooper
summary: Alix Earle spoke about the Alex Cooper drama on her new Netflix show. Here’s what happened and what she said when breaking her silence.
story: Alix Earle is using her new Netflix reality show, “Earle Meets World,” to break her silence on the alleged falling out between her and “Call Her Daddy” host Alex Cooper.
Earle rose to fame in 2020 when she began posting “Get Ready With Me” content. Since then, Earle’s platform has amassed over 8 million TikTok followers, and she’s also launched a skincare company.

In 2023, Earle also signed a podcast deal with Cooper’s media company, The Unwell Network. But Earle and her podcast were dropped in early 2025. No reasoning was given beyond official statements from reps. The internet suspected a possible rift between the two, and evidence was given during some social media exchanges in spring of this year.
Earle, speaking to TODAY.com ahead of the show’s release, says the “social media storm” surfaced during the last month of filming “Earle Meets World.”
“It just kind of naturally got brought up, and was a natural thing happening in my life, and we decided to just lean into it,” Earle says.
What Happened Between Alex Cooper and Alix Earle?
That’s the thing: It wasn’t exactly clear. The business relationship severed in 2025, and then began a series of posts that appeared to be directed at each other into the following year.
On April 11, 2026, Earle reposted a video on TikTok in which one user called Cooper “an ambulance chaser.”
Cooper then addressed the situation head-on in a TikTok on April 13.

“Hi guys. You guys know I don’t usually address this kind of stuff because it feels like a waste of time, and honestly it’s embarrassing to participate in this,” Cooper said. “But I am obviously seeing the videos, I’m getting tagged, I see the DMs, I see the comments, so at this point it just feels long overdue.
“Alix Earle, hey girl, the passive-aggressive reposts and the likes and the commenting on things, I gotta call you out here,” she added.
Until recently, Earle had been tight-lipped.
She replied to Earle’s video with a comment that said, “Ok on it!!” Then, when she stopped by TODAY in May, Craig Melvin asked about the “beef.” Earle said the drama was “exaggerated” online.
The Netflix show gives a behind-the-scenes look at how Earle chose to respond and what she said.
In Episode 1 of “Earle Meets World,” Earle’s father, TJ Earle, who is also her manager, brings up the situation.
“You at some point are obligated to set the record straight,” he told her. “The question is, ‘When’s the right time?’ ‘When and where?’”
What Does Alix Earle Say About the Rift in the Netflix Show?
Here’s what Earle said about two of the main aspects of her relationship with Cooper: Earle’s “Call Her Daddy” appearance in 2023 and the rift with Unwell.
TODAY.com has reached out to Cooper for comment.

In conversation with her “dadager” in the premiere episode, Earle said she feels Cooper betrayed her and took advantage of her position of power as an older, more established creator when she invited her on “Call Her Daddy.”

“That was on my dream board for years, I was like, ‘Yay!’ It felt very personal, like she was going to be an older sister and look out for me. So it was a really exciting time for me,” Earle said in Episode 1. “She sold me on a dream that she was going to protect me and look out for me, and I feel like she took advantage of my admiration of her.”
When Earle appeared on “Call Her Daddy,” she spoke in detail about topics like her sex life, which she said she wasn’t “comfortable” with.

“From the start, I didn’t realize things were going wrong because I was obsessed with her. This is my idol. I’m so happy to work with her,” Earle said in the finale. “Then, I constantly felt taken advantage of and used and mistreated and manipulated. We were filming her podcast and she’s having us drink before and asking me really sexual questions I wasn’t comfortable with, but I’m also answering because I’m drunk.”
She also spoke about father’s very public affair with Ashley Dupré, now his wife, and how it affected the whole family. Dupré, in Episode 3, addressed the podcast directly.

“It bought up so many things from my past and my family’s past. It was so embarrassing for me to go through all that,” she said. “For conversations that I have to have with my little kids, to their parents seeing it ... to relive all those traumas really took its toll on me.”

Dupré and Earle had a heart-to-heart at the end of the episode, revealing the toll the episode took on the family. Earle said the family group chat was deleted and they needed therapy to start talking again.
In the season finale, Earle gave her side of what went wrong with their professional partnership and the podcast deal.

“They were a startup company at the time, so things weren’t going to go great, but there were just constantly issues,” she said. “It wasn’t run properly and it wasn’t what I was promised or told that it was going to be like working with them.”
TJ Earle also explained some of the “issues” from a manager standpoint, saying that there were no real resources given to Earle’s podcast production.

“(Alix) was doing it by herself, traveling around with suitcases full of cameras, doing it herself. So you have the show, the revenue coming in from the show, and then the expenses get taken out of the revenue, and what’s leftover is your profit, which gets split between Alix and Unwell. There was no expenses because they had Alix doing everything,” he said.
Later in the “Earle Meets World” finale, Earle asked Dupré and her father for advice on a text she drafted to send to Cooper, but never actually sent. She read the lengthy text word-for-word.

“I wanted to write you directly and let you know I don’t like you. I’m not going to fall for your bait of getting into a back-and-forth online and I don’t think you want that either. You are manipulative and toxic. Go ahead and say ‘it’s just business’ all you want, but the way you approach business is disgusting,” Earle read. “You choose money over morals. You took advantage of me at a young age in a new industry I knew nothing about. You are full of false promises, and Unwell was a continuation of that.”
In the text, Earle also said Cooper threatened her once things went south.

“We had a call where you threatened me to not go to war with you, because you know how sick and twisted you are,” Earle said. “Go ahead, share this, use it against me, but you will no longer scare or trap me. You’re right, I may be petty, but I’m not malicious. If there’s one thing I learned from doing business with you, it’s to never do business with anyone like you.”
Why Alix Earle Is Opening Up Now
Earle explains to TODAY.com what went into the decision to ultimately not only include the situation, but to go as far as reading the text message to the world.

“I was, like, you know what? This is the reality and the things going on in my life. I didn’t want to put out a show where we’re skipping over a chunk of time because I wanted to hold myself back. I think being able to have the cameras there and see my family supporting me, you don’t really get to see that online.”
Earle looks at “Earle Meets World” as a chance for her followers to get a closer look at how her familial support system comes into play when pressing post is not so easy.

“It’s a little stressful sometimes when you’re dealing with something like that, at that scale, it’s not so easy to upload and post something,” Earle says. “So I think it really shows how my family’s there to support me in those decisions, even when I’m, like, spiraling, and I’m not sure what to do.”
Now that she’s spoken up, she’s ready to move on.

“I don’t even think it’s really about, like, giving a definitive answer, or getting into it like a ‘he said, she said,’ or like, point by point,” Earle says. “I said my piece, and I have closed that chapter.”

title: Bunnie XO Tells Jenna Bush Hager Why She ‘Still Wants to Have a Baby’ After Jelly Roll Breakup
summary: Bunnie XO is opening up about her desire to become a mom later in life.
story: Bunnie XO is opening up about her desire to become a mom later in life.

The podcaster and bestselling author has spoken candidly over the years about wanting to have a child, previously sharing in 2024 that she and now-estranged husband Jelly Roll had started their IVF journey. But in May, the singer filed for divorce from Bunnie XO, ahead of their 10-year anniversary.

Even though the two are no longer together, Bunnie XO told Jenna Bush Hager on the latest episode of the TODAY co-host’s “Open Book” podcast that she hasn’t given up on her dream and has been inspired by another celebrity who had her first child in her 40s.
When Jenna asked if Bunnie XO, 46, still wants to have a baby after her public and difficult breakup, she swiftly replied, “Yes!”
“You know who inspired me a lot more too is freaking Cameron Diaz,” she said. “She just had her third child at like 53!”
Bunnie XO pointed out that Diaz welcomed her first child with husband Benji Madden when she was 47.
“I think that’s so inspiring, and I feel like it gives you a purpose later on in life to live for,” Bunnie XO explained. “So yeah…I will still have a baby.”
Bunnie was a stepmom to Jelly Roll’s two children from previous relationships: 18-year-old daughter Bailee Ann DeFord and 10-year-old son Noah Buddy DeFord.
She told Jenna that as she enters this new chapter, she will likely focus on protecting her privacy. She still plans to be open and honest with her fans while also setting boundaries.
“I just feel like I need to keep it close to my chest, especially right now, because everybody just wants to pin like the craziest stuff on me,” she added. “But it’s still a dream.”
Previously, the “Dumb Blonde” podcast host spoke with Jenna about life post-divorce and raising a child during her appearance on TODAY with Jenna and Sheinelle Aug. 20.
She told Jenna and Sheinelle Jones that she is viewing her split from Jelly Roll with a glass half full perspective.

“I know when something like that that’s deeply personal happens, it’s beautifully tragic, but at the same time there’s always a silver lining, there’s always something better to look forward to,” she shared. “There’s so much more to talk about with me especially, and with women, than their past lovers and people in their lives.”

While Bunnie XO said on the now-deleted June 18 episode of her podcast that she and Jelly Roll will co-parent together, she revealed to Jenna and Sheinelle during her Aug. appearance that she’s not sure if he will be included in her future plans.
She added that she will document her journey to motherhood in her next book.
“I can’t wait for you guys to read about it because it’s been one hell of a journey, let me tell you,” she said.

title: From Jane Fonda to Miss Piggy, Celebrities Share Moving Tributes To Gloria Steinem
summary: Tributes are pouring in from celebrities across an array of fields for the trailblazing feminist icon Gloria Steinem, who died Sept. 2.
story: Tributes are pouring in from celebrities across an array of fields for the trailblazing feminist icon Gloria Steinem, who died Sept. 2.

Prominent voices across sports, entertainment and more have shared emotional words about the impact that the journalist and activist, who dedicated her life to championing women’s rights, had on their lives and the greater movement towards gender equality. The messages follow Steinem’s passing, “surrounded by some of the many who loved her,” according to an announcement shared on her official Instagram account.

“She had a clever, often funny way to say just what was needed to surface feelings and ideas about where we belonged, what our inchoate yearnings meant, whether power was a word that women could and should embrace for ourselves, and how different power looked when held in men’s hands alone,” actor and fellow outspoken women’s rights activist Jane Fonda, who co-founded the Women’s Media Center with Steinem and writer Robin Morgan, wrote in an Instagram post.
Fonda added that Steinem “lives on in the changed lives of many women who don’t consider themselves feminists or part of the women’s movement.”

“I’ve met many such women who because of what Gloria said or wrote gained the courage to leave bad marriages, start their own businesses, persuade husbands to help with household chores,” Fonda said in the post.
Steinem died “peacefully at her home in New York City,” according to the Instagram post shared on her official account. She was 92.

During her decades in the spotlight, Steinem left a significant cultural imprint on American society. And today, she is largely considered one of the faces of the second-wave of feminism — one that broadened the fight for equal rights from a focus on the right to vote to also include issues like employment, politics, education and sexuality.

Skyrocketing to national prominence in 1963, Steinem made a name for herself after going undercover as a Playboy bunny and publishing a two-part exposé on the working conditions and treatment of women at the controversial New York Playboy Club. In 1971, she launched the groundbreaking feminist outlet Ms. magazine, which became one of the first women-led publications to tackle heavy issues like domestic violence and abortion.

For decades, Steinem continued her work, co-founding several other organizations including the National Women’s Political Caucus, the Women’s Action Alliance and the Ms. Foundation for Women along with the Women’s Media Center.
From television host Andy Cohen to the fabulous Muppet queen Miss Piggy, celebrities honored the outspoken activist for her undeniable contributions to society.
Here’s a look at how prominent figures across industries are mourning Steinem’s death and celebrating her legacy.
Jane Fonda
Fonda, who collaborated with Steinem for decades, shared details of the late activist’s life, including the way in which she “built the new women’s movement.”

“Gloria, in her graceful, kind, and deeply intelligent way, changed the world we live in,” Fonda wrote. “For decades, she trudged through every airport in the country, in sandals and a trench, carrying her own suitcase, packed with a few black clothes, hair curlers, and steam iron, in order to speak to women — at conferences, town halls, consciousness raising groups. No group was too small to deserve Gloria’s time.”
Lena Dunham
Writer and “Girls” creator Lena Dunham shared personal memories she had of the activist, including some particularly moving anecdotes on how Steinem took her under her wing.

“You let me wander in as a lost twenty something, determined that things should change and unsure how or if they could, and you advised me on everything from men (can be fun, aren’t required) to activism (it’s a marathon, not a race.),” Dunham recalled.
Miss Piggy

The iconic Muppet Miss Piggy posted an emotional message on Instagram in remembrance of Steinem, whom she shared a evening of conversation during the 2015 Sackler Center First Awards. That night, Miss Piggy was honored as a feminist icon herself.

“Throughout her incredible life, Gloria broke glass ceilings, challenged perceptions, and fiercely advocated for women around the world,” Piggy wrote. “Few people have inspired and influenced moi more than dear Gloria, and I will forever treasure the fabulous times we shared together.”
Oprah
Oprah Winfrey shared post on Instagram, recounting a 2012 event in which the two spoke to young women at Barnard College.
“I was proud to bear witness to their sense of worthiness and independence—and recognized how Gloria’s work had helped forge the path to that moment,” she wrote.
Winfrey also mentioned that Steinem “leaves us with more freedom than she inherited and with the responsibility to keep widening that freedom for the women and girls who come next.”
Billie Jean King

Tennis icon Billie Jean King, who was featured in the first version of Ms. magazine, shared on social media that the world “has lost a true giant and a dynamic voice.” King, whose 1973 win against Bobby Riggs in the “Battle of the Sexes” match became a symbol of women’s empowerment, praised Steinem for her indefatigable spirit.
“She devoted her life to the pursuit of equality and political change, working tirelessly for over 70 years to ensure each generation built upon the work of the previous one,” King wrote.
Meghan Markle

The former Meghan Markle, whose official title is Duchess of Sussex, shared a post on Instagram about Steinem, whom she considered a “friend and mentor.” Markle, whose highly publicized marriage to Prince Harry has long been the subject of tabloid fodder, shared that Steinem had a close relationship with her family and often helped her during difficult times.

“Publicly, we did interviews together, called young voters to encourage them to have their voices heard, attended award ceremonies, and brainstormed how to help this beautiful yet complicated world to become more equitable,” Markle recalled in her post.

She added that “privately, she was even better than you would imagine- spending Thanksgiving with our family, introducing me to one of my best friends (forever the champion of female friendship), loving our children with her whole heart, counseling me during hard times, and giving extraordinary advice and perspective with a cup of tea and an unrivaled cheekiness and wit.”
Andy Cohen

Bravo icon Andy Cohen shared a hilarious story about how he once invited Steinem to his talk show “Watch What Happens Live” in 2015 to discuss the reality show personalities in his “Real Housewives” franchise. And he had a pretty perfect description of not only what went down, but also of the activist.
“She absolutely ATE ME ALIVE,” he joked. “What an incredible human with a legacy that will outlive us all.

title: Ms. Magazine Pays Tribute To Gloria Steinem, Its Revolutionary Founder
summary: As the world honors trailblazing feminist, journalist and activist Gloria Steinem, who died this week, the groundbreaking magazine she founded more than a half century ago has paid tribute to the icon.
story: As the world honors trailblazing feminist, journalist and activist Gloria Steinem, who died this week, the groundbreaking magazine she founded more than a half century ago has paid tribute to the icon.

Ms. magazine, which Steinem launched in the 1970s as an answer to a media landscape that largely catered to male interests and relegated women to lifestyle issues, published a moving obituary about the revolutionary founder. It comes hours after it was announced that Steinem had died Sept. 2 in her New York City home, according to a post on her official Instagram page. She was 92.
In the obituary, executive editor Kathy Spillar wrote about the ways in which Steinem “transformed journalism, feminism and the possibilities women could imagine for themselves.”

“For more than half a century, the public knew her as one of feminism’s most recognizable figures: the writer with the center-parted hair and aviator glasses; the assured speaker at rallies, campuses and conventions; the tireless traveler who carried the movement’s ideas into living rooms and union halls, onto television screens and into the corridors of political power,” Spillar wrote in the tribute published Sept. 3. “But Steinem understood something the culture surrounding her often did not: Movements are never made by one person.”

Steinem “passed away peacefully at her home in New York City, surrounded by some of the many who loved her,” according to the Instagram post on her official page. The post did not give a cause of death.

Her women-run magazine, which released its first standalone issue in 1972, continues to publish in print as well as digitally. And much like it did at its inception, the outlet covers stories ranging from women’s health, democracy and culture.

Spillar, who helms the publication, wrote in the tribute that Steinem, who tirelessly championed causes ranging from reproductive rights to eradicating workplace inequalities, fought to elevate intersectionality in the women’s movement.

“She insisted that feminism’s history include the Black women, labor organizers, Indigenous women, lesbians, civil rights leaders and community activists whose work had too often been erased,” Spillar wrote, adding that Steinem often credited figures of all backgrounds —  including Shirley Chisolm, the first Black woman to be elected to the United States Congress and civil rights leader and voting rights activist Fannie Lou Hamer — as influences and teachers.

Spillar added that when “the media attempted to anoint her the leader of a leaderless movement, she redirected attention toward the organizers, coalitions and collective action that made change possible.”

Steinem first rose to national prominence in 1963 after going undercover as a Playboy bunny and producing a two-part exposé on the working conditions and treatment of women at the infamous New York Playboy Club.

“The investigation made her famous, but it also temporarily made editors less willing to take her seriously,” Spillar wrote. “That experience taught Steinem a lasting lesson about who determines which stories count as news, and about the cost women pay when men control the institutions that assign, edit, finance and distribute those stories.”

In 1971, Steinem started Ms. as an insert in New York Magazine. At the time, the media environment was heavily skewed toward male consumers, Steinem said, and that there were “no other magazines for women that weren’t about food, fashion and family.”

“I believed that advertisers would soon realize that women’s interests were just as wide and deep as men’s interests are and there would be new magazines that were at least like, say, Esquire for women,” she wrote in a 2023 book about the magazine in celebration of its 50th anniversary.

The insert found almost instant success and sold 300,000 copies in under one week. It contained rarely covered topics from domestic violence to abortion. The groundbreaking preview also included a list of women, including Steinem herself, who admitted to having abortions before they were federally legalized through 1973’s Roe v. Wade decision. The list featured names from Anaïs Nin to Billie Jean King.

The preview itself was highly controversial. CBS “60 Minutes” host Harry Reasoner, for example, famously said, “I’ll give it six months before they run out of things to say.” Years later, Reasoner apologized for the remark. Syndicated columnist James Kilpatrick called the work a note of “petulance, of bitchiness, or nervous fingernails screeching across a blackboard.”

By the next year, Steinem’s publication released its first standalone issue. The cover featured superhero Wonder Woman with the headline “Wonder Woman for President,” in part a commentary on DC Comics’ decision to remove the character’s superpowers. An essay about Wonder Woman’s feminist impact in the issue prompted the comic book giant to restore her powers.

As years went by, the magazine became a major vehicle for the second wave of feminism, of which many saw Steinem as one of the faces. In contrast to the earlier wave, this newer movement expanded the push for equality to a broader range of issues in society from employment to politics to sexuality.
Today, the outlet stands as “an independent, nonprofit feminist,” Spillar wrote.

“Ms. is not owned by a billionaire or beholden to commercial advertisers. It is an independent, nonprofit feminist newsroom sustained by Ms. partners, readers and donors,” Spillar wrote. “That model allows us to investigate stories advertisers may find inconvenient, to center people commercial media consider insufficiently profitable and to report on women not as a demographic niche but as full human beings whose freedom is inseparable from democracy.”
Spillar called on readers to support independent media, an indelible part of Steinem’s legacy.

“The most important monument to Gloria will not be a statue, an award or even a shelf of remarkable books. It will be the work we— working together — do next,” Spillar wrote. “It will be every person who organizes instead of surrendering to isolation. Every journalist who asks whose voice is missing. Every reader who supports independent media. Every young person who discovers that an injustice bearing down on their life is neither natural nor inevitable. That’s how the circle grows wider.”
She concluded, writing that Steinem “changed the story women were permitted to tell about themselves.
“Now it is our responsibility to keep telling the truth — and to make certain that no billionaire, advertiser, government or algorithm can silence it,” Spillar wrote.

title: Dolly Parton’s Nieces Recall Their Last Moments With Her: ‘We Were Just Regular Girls’
summary: From giving career pep talks to gabbing about her favorite fast food, Dolly Parton was just one of the “regular girls” when spending time with her nieces.
story: From giving career pep talks to gabbing about her favorite fast food, Dolly Parton was just one of the “regular girls” when spending time with her nieces.

Heidi Parton and Danielle Parton, daughters of Dolly Parton’s younger brothers Randy and Robert Jr., respectively, shared some sweet memories of their late aunt on TODAY Sept. 3, while also showing some of the country singer’s trademark humor.
The two spoke from the family’s hometown of Sevierville, Tennessee, as they remembered the last time they spent together with their aunt in person.
Heidi Parton recalled getting advice from her aunt after releasing her latest country album “Reflections” in 2025.

“I sat down and had a very sweet, in-depth conversation about how to proceed with my career,” she said. “We talked for about an hour and she was like, ‘Baby, I’m just going to tell you this. You’ve got the talent. If you want it, go get it.’ I’m like, ‘Yes ma’am.’

“We had a really good conversation,” she continued. “She was just so sweet and so supportive, and it was just really precious because I hadn’t gotten to do that in so long. I really just hold that very close to me now.”

Danielle Parton, 50, shares a January birthday with her aunt, and she recalled them having lunch together in February to celebrate. Legendary actor Robert Duvall had recently died at 95 at the time, and Danielle asked Dolly if she knew him.

“We were discussing about who passed and I said, ‘Have you met him?’ And she’s like ‘Oh yeah, he’s precious,’” Danielle Parton,  said. “We were talking about different stars and how interesting it is that she’s got to meet all these other people, and I said, ‘Do you ever think of yourself as famous? How do you see yourself?’
“She goes, ‘Oh, no.’ She goes, ‘I’m still the same kid I was growing up poor,’” she added. And she really did.”
She also remembered the two talking about one of their favorite subjects.

“She liked regular food. Oh, she was a fast food junkie,” Danielle said. “... We were always talking about our food and stuff. We were just regular girls, and we were talking about regular stuff, and just life.”
Aunt Dolly also gave Danielle, a pilot and owner of the moonshine distillery Shine Girl, business advice as well.
“She was good about, ‘Trust your gut. You know what’s right for you and don’t let anybody sway you from it,’” she said.

Danielle Parton was one of a handful of family members who attended a small ceremony laying the country music icon to rest in Nashville alongside her husband of 59 years, Carl Dean, who died at 82 in 2025.
“It was very, very private,” Danielle Parton said. “I don’t even know if I was supposed to be there, I just happened to be in town when all this took place.”
She said in total, there were about 10 people in attendance. Dolly Parton’s first cousin Richie Owens said on TODAY Sept. 3 he was also among the attendees.

“Not even close to anywhere near all of us. She was beautiful and peaceful and to me, I don’t know if I want to say healing, but she was beautiful and she was at peace, and so that helped me be at peace with it,” she said.
Dolly Parton was rarely at rest in her life as a writer, singer, philanthropist, business owner and more.

“If there’s anybody that deserved a little peace in their life, it’s her because she never had a moment’s peace, ever,” Danielle Parton said. “If you ever thought, ‘Well I just want to meet her,’ well, times that by like 10 million and that’s how many people always just wanted to meet her, just wanted to say hi. And then she had all of us driving her crazy all the time.”

title: Jenna Bush Hager Says Her September 2026 Read With Jenna Pick Is By One of Her ‘Absolute Favorites’
summary: Read With Jenna’s September 2026 title is The Witches of Cambridge by Alice Hoffmna.
story: Spooky season came a bit early this year thanks to Jenna Bush Hager’s September 2026 Read With Jenna pick: “The Witches of Cambridge” by Alice Hoffman.
“I cannot think of a more perfect book to welcome us to fall,” Jenna said, calling Hoffman one of her “absolute favorites.”

Hoffman is the author of over 30 books, but she’s most famous for her witches. Her famous “Practical Magic” series inspired the cult classic movie of the same name starring Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock. The sequel, “Practical Magic 2,” based on Hoffman’s 2021 novel “The Book of Magic,” will hit theaters Sept. 10.
“The Witches of Cambridge” follows the tradition set by “Practical Magic”: Young women discovering their powers and their relationships with each other.

The book is set in 1950s Cambridge and follows two Radcliffe College students who are inducted into a secret society for witches, called the Lilith Society. One, Lauren, knows all about her heritage and bloodline; the other, Ava, is a stranger to her powers, and knows only that she feels out of place in the world.
“They quickly realize the witch trials of the past may not be as deeply buried as they once believed. It’s a novel about love, friendship and finding your power,” Jenna said.
"The Witches of Cambridge" by Alice Hoffman
Speaking to TODAY.com, Hoffman said the book began when she took a professional detour and attended the Harvard Divinity School.
“To this day I’m not exactly sure why I did it, and I’m so glad that I did it,” she says.
During what she called her “toughest class,” Theories and Methods, she was tasked with writing a paper about someone at Harvard she disagreed with.

“I asked her if I could do it as fiction. I knew right away who I was going to pick: The Mather family,” she said, explaining that Increase Mather, a former president of Harvard, and his son Cotton Mather had “not been friendly to witches.”
Puritan ministers Increase and Cotton Mather both had ties to the Salem Witch Trials.

Meanwhile, Hoffman was influenced by her classmates at the Harvard Divinity School, describing them as “young people who were searching and looking to restart their lives.” And after years living in Massachusetts, she felt for the first time immersed in Harvard. “It felt like there’s a whole other world that you know regular people don’t see,” she says.
And so, “The Witches of Cambridge” was born.
To Hoffman, who has written about witches in the past, a witch is a woman “who has power and who is not afraid.”
Don’t expect the same kind of story as you’ll find in “Practical Magic” series and its prequels, though.
Where “Practical Magic” is about sisters, Hoffman says “this book was more about situations with friends.”

“How important friendship is for women, and how deep it is for women. I’m not really sure what it’s like for men, but for women, sometimes I think it’s more important than romantic relationships,” she says.

She compares female friendship, fittingly, to a coven. And it’s one she doesn’t quite want to leave. Hoffman shares that she’s already working on her next book — a sequel to “The Witches of Cambridge.”
“I think there’s more to the story, so that’s been fun,” she says.

title: Bunnie XO Says She Had to Be ‘Picked Off the Floor,’ Ate Baby Food ‘To Get By’ From Heartbreak from Jelly Roll Breakup
summary: Bunnie XO shared that she “wasn’t eating” and lost 20 pounds in the aftermath of husband Jelly Roll filing for divorce.
story: Bunnie XO shared that she “wasn’t eating” and lost 20 pounds in the aftermath of husband Jelly Roll filing for divorce.

The “Dumb Blonde” podcaster and bestselling author opened up on the Sept. 3 episode of Jenna Bush Hager’s “Open Book” podcast about how she struggled when her husband of nearly 10 years filed for divorce on May 18, according to court records from Williamson County, Tennessee.

“There was moments when my team had to pick me up off the floor and give me IVs,” she said. “Because I wasn’t eating. I was eating baby food to get by. I lost 20 pounds. Heartbreak, man, it’s the best freaking diet.”

Jelly Roll, a Grammy-winning country singer whose real name is Jason DeFord, filed for divorce two months before what would’ve been the couple’s 10th wedding anniversary. He cited irreconcilable differences as the reason for the split, according to the court filing.
He and Bunnie XO each spoke out separately about the divorce filing.
“I don’t want people to think I’m just out here like just acting like she doesn’t hurt,” she told Jenna. “Yeah, it hurt. And I talked about it, and I let viewers in.”
On the June 18 episode of her “Dumb Blonde Podcast,” Bunnie XO confirmed the split. She also said it was “not mutual” and not her choice to break up.
Bunnie XO, whose real name is Alisa DeFord, has since deleted that episode of her podcast.
“I didn’t want to live in it,” she told Jenna. “You guys got your headlines, you guys got your clips.”
She noted how snippets of her podcast were all over social media for anyone wanting to see her talking about her divorce, but she didn’t want to relive the episode.

“I just didn’t want to live in it, and I don’t feel like I had to,” she said. “I said what I needed to say, I made a s---load of money off of it. If I was going to do it for money, I would’ve left it up. Every time I went to my YouTube, I didn’t want to see that.

“And also I don’t want to be the freakin’ poster child for divorce,” she continued. “There’s nothing hot about that. It’s a very devastating situation anybody has to go through. Families get broken up, hearts get broken. It’s time to move on.”
Bunnie XO spoke on TODAY Aug. 20 about living the single life again and trying to move forward.

“And I just hope my journey can show people, ‘Hey, you know what, no matter how hard the situation you’re going through, you’re going get through that, you’re going to rise up, and you’re going to be an even better version of yourself,” she told Jenna and Sheinelle Jones.
Once she shared her side of the breakup on her podcast, she was ready to look forward and not back.
“Everybody loves to watch a trainwreck, and I was not going to participate in that circus,” she said on Jenna’s podcast. “I am my own person, I stand on my own two feet.
“I don’t see why I couldn’t continue to stand on my own two feet and not have to dwell in that space of emotion.”

title: ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Cast 2026: Who’s Competing on Season 35
summary: A new crew of celebrities is gearing up to hit the ballroom floor for Season 35 of “Dancing With the Stars.” Here’s what to know.
story: A new crew of celebrities is gearing up to hit the ballroom floor for Season 35 of “Dancing With the Stars.”
On Sept. 2, the full cast and their partners competing for the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy were announced, with a slew of surprising names.
Returning as co-hosts are Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough, with Carrie Ann Inaba, Derek Hough and Bruno Tonioli as judges.

Months ahead of the cast reveal, “Traitors” and “Love Island UK” star Maura Higgins and “Summer House” star Ciara Miller were announced as part of the cast. Last month, it was also announced that Witney Carson, who’s pregnant with baby No. 3, is partnered with Jimmy Kimmel’s sidekick Guillermo Rodriguez.
Mark Ballas who is partnered with Higgins tells TODAY.com the upcoming season “should be a fun one. It seems like a good group.”

Also joining the cast this year as a pro is the winner of “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro.” The spinoff series, which premiered on July 13, saw 12 dancers compete for a chance to become the next professional on Season 35 of “DWTS.”
The winner Adele Zaikman will make her debut as a pro with “Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” star Connor Leavitt.

“We’re excited to see what she does on this coming season,” Ballas, who was a judge on “The Next Pro,” tells TODAY.com about Zaikman’s debut. “Her skill set is undeniable. So now she’s gonna have to take that journey ... transitioning from the competition world into the television world. But I believe she can get there.”
See the full “Dancing With the Stars” Season 35 cast and their pros, below.
Tyler Cameron and Sharna Burgess

Tyler Cameron first captured viewers’ attention when he appeared on Hannah Brown’s season (Season 15) of “The Bachelorette.” He has since focused on his real estate and construction background, starring in his Prime Video series “Going Home with Tyler Cameron” and judging HGTV’s “Bachelor Mansion Takeover.”
Guillermo Rodriguez and Witney Carson

Guillermo Rodriguez previously worked in a parking lot as a security guard for “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” He was discovered and has been working with the show for over 23 years. He frequently pops up at red carpet events to interview celebs for the show. He also recently released his own brand of fresh salsa, Guillermo’s Salsa.
Taylor Hanson and Britt Stewart
Taylor Hanson is best known for forming the band Hanson with his brothers Isaac and Zac in 1992. The band released major hits like “MMMBop” and has received three Grammy nominations.
Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik

Tatyana Ali first became a household name when she portrayed Ashley in “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air.” She has been in the industry for over 40 years, also showing off her talents on the Broadway stage and her debut album “Kiss the Sky.” She currently has a recurring role on “Abbott Elementary.”
Sarah Jane Nader and Hailey Bills

Sarah Jane Nader is the star of reality television series “Love Thy Nader,” which also follows her sister and “DWTS” alum Brooks Nader. Sarah Jane Nader is an actor and model who has appeared in campaigns for MAC Cosmetics, Alice + Olivia and other brands.
Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas

Maura Higgins is ready to swap her “thinking caps” for her dancing shoes. Higgins delighted fans across the pond when she appeared on Season 5 (or Series in the U.K.) of the flagship “Love Island” series. She then made her way stateside and hosted “Love Island USA: Aftersun” and “Love Island Games: Aftersun.” She finished as a runner-up on the latest season of the hit series “The Traitors,” where she played with fellow Faithful Mark Ballas.
Ciara Miller and Brandon Armstrong

Ciara Miller is a former ICU nurse who is best known for starring on Bravo’s “Summer House.” She also appeared on Season 3 of “The Traitors” and spent this summer co-hosting “Love Island USA: Aftersun.”
Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson

Gleeks! Get ready to tune in to watch Harry Shum Jr. compete. Fans fells in love with Shum when he played Mike Chang on “Glee.” He recently starred in the hit Netflix rom-com “Voicemails for Isabelle” and currently plays Dr. Benson Blue Kwan on “Grey’s Anatomy.” Some of his other credits include “Crazy Rich Asians” and “Everything Everywhere All at Once.”
Jackson Olson and Emma Slater
Jackson Olson is a second baseman for the Savannah Bananas. Off the field, he keeps fans entertained on social media with his baseball insights, food finds at the ballpark and his personal life.
Jenna Dewan and Valentin Chmerkovskiy

Fans first became captivated by Jenna Dewan’s talent when she starred in the 2006 dance flick “Step Up.” She currently stars with Nathan Fillion in “The Rookie” She joined the show as a guest star in Season 3, became a series regular in Season 4 and has been on series ever since.
Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach

Track star Ezra Frech had fans all over America cheering for him when he competed at the 2024 Paris Paralympic Games, winning gold medals in both the 100 meter and high jump. Frech competes in the long jump, as well, and was the youngest member of the U.S. Paralympic team at the 2020 Tokyo Paralympic Games at just 16 years old.
Julia Stiles and Ezra Sosa

Actor Julia Stiles is ready to take over the ballroom floor. Stiles, who recently made her feature directorial debut with “Wish You Were Here,” has landed Emmy and Golden Globe nominations. Her credits include “10 Things I Hate About You,” “Save the Last Dane,” “Silver Linings Playbook, “Hustlers” and the “Bourne” franchise.
Giada De Laurentiis and Alan Bersten

Giada De Laurentiis is an Emmy-winning chef and New York Times bestselling author. She trained at Le Cordon Bleu in Paris and previously hosted Food Network’s “Everyday Italian” before landing other series like “Giada at Home” and “Giada in Italy.” She has made multiple appearances on TODAY, showing off tasty recipes.
Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold

Comedian Connor Wood has been making millions of fans on the internet laugh with his funny short-form videos. Variety named him on its 2025 Comedy Impact Report, which also featured Conan O’Brien, Nathan Fielder and Nikki Glaser.
Conner Leavitt and Adele Zaikman

Conner Leavitt, husband to Season 34 contestant Whitney Leavitt, appears on Hulu’s “Secret Lives of Mormon Wives.” He also has a performance background, as he starred in the off-Broadway production of “11 to Midnight.”
Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov

Figure skater Amber Glenn is an Olympic gold medalist and three-time U.S. national champion. This year, she and Team USA won Olympic gold in figure skating and she became the first U.S. woman to land three triple axels at a single Olympic Games, cementing her spot in the history books.

title: Jason Kelce Says Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift Ditched This Wedding Tradition — and It Made It ‘So Fun’
summary: Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce discuss on “New Heights” what made Travis’s wedding to Taylor Swift such a success.
story: You may have heard that Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce got married at Madison Square Garden earlier this summer. What you may not have heard is how the event, which was attended by stars from all walks of life, went down.

In the Sept. 2 season premiere of Kelce’s “New Heights” podcast, which he hosts with brother Jason Kelce, the siblings opened up about that July 3 evening and the one tweak that made it even more of a success.

“The thing I really liked about this wedding in particular and the way you guys structured it was after all that was done, there wasn’t the sit-down formal stuff,” Jason Kelce said. “There wasn’t a bunch of the speeches. It was just time to party and have fun. And that’s what made it so fun to for me to be there.”
Guests were not allowed to have their phones, which changed the dynamics of the night.
“With no phones comes people not having to be on guard and like, feel that something, whatever that feeling is for everyone,” Travis Kelce said.

“It makes everyone be in the moment and be present. And it was so cool seeing everyone from my childhood not only mesh with Taylor and her childhood and her family and friends and people that she works with, to who we’ve come encounter with over our career and who we just admire as people and have become good friends with now.”
Travis Kelce, who said the night was something he and Swift “will never forget,” was also awed by hearing how the guests felt about the wedding.

“It’s just been so cool to see that world come together and hear through, person by person, after the wedding, just how awesome of a time everyone had there,” he said. “And that’s what we wanted it to be. We wanted it to be a beautiful ceremony, but we also wanted to make sure that everybody left there having some fun. And it was a magical night.”

The pair also had high praise for Adam Sandler, who officiated the nuptials. Travis Kelce said the comedian got ordained in New York and called him “the best person on the planet,” while his brother said, “The ceremony was beautiful. Adam killed it.”

Travis Kelce and Swift haven’t said much publicly about their wedding since they exchanged vows. Before “New Heights,” Travis Kelce made a brief comment at a Chiefs’ training camp press conference, calling the nuptials “the best night of my life.”
“I wish it could have lasted even longer than it did. It felt like it just happened at a blink of an eye,” he said on “New Heights.”
He also thanked Madison Square Garden for holding the event and meeting their needs.

“We wanted to do it somewhere where we could have a very intimate and genuine setting without a lot of distractions. And we needed it to be a private feel,” he said. “And MSG went above and beyond to give us that.”

title: Where Is Raygun, Australia’s Breakdancer Who Went Viral At The Paris Olympics, Now? She Just Gave an Update
summary: Australian breakdancer Raygun just gave an update on her life two years after her viral Olympics.
story: Raygun has returned to the dance floor.
The Australian breakdancer set social media on fire with her viral performances at the 2024 Olympics in Paris, unleashing a torrent of posts ridiculing her skills.
Two years later, she has shared an update on her life and her Olympic ordeal in the new documentary “Raygun: Breaking Badly,” which is part of Netflix’s “Untold” series.
“I went out there and performed, and I didn’t do as well as I hoped, and then the world freaked out,” Gunn says in the film.
Here is what to know about her story and how she is doing now.
Who Is Raygun?
Raygun is the name used for breaking competitions by Australian Olympian Rachael Gunn.
At the time of the 2024 Olympics, she was a lecturer at Sydney’s Macquarie University with a Ph.D. in Cultural Studies, according to CNBC.
Breaking was introduced as an Olympic sport at the 2024 Games, and Gunn was the women’s qualifier from the Oceania region after winning a competition in Sydney.

She gained notoriety with her two performances in Paris in which she did not earn a single point from the judges across four rounds, losing by a combined 36-0 to two competitors. One particular move in which she mimicked a kangaroo in honor of her native country was turned into a meme.

Social media videos across multiple platforms mocked Gunn’s skills and questioned how she qualified for the Olympics. It brought to life a fear leading up to the Games that she says she shared with her therapist.
“She was like, ‘What’s the worst that could happen?’” Gunn says in the Netflix documentary.
“The worst that could happen is that the whole world could laugh at me,” Gunn says she replied.
“She’s like, ‘Do you think that’s reasonable?’” Gunn says her therapist answered.
An Australian B-girl who goes by Flix says in the Netflix show that she was “offended” and “embarrassed” by Gunn’s performance in Paris.

Another B-girl who goes by Tinylocks, who had previously beaten Gunn in competition, says in the documentary that she told her friends after Gunn’s performance that Gunn was “going to need psychological support.”

Gunn, 38, also shared the strange sensation of realizing she was going viral for all the wrong reasons. Adele was talking about it on stage at one of her concerts, and an NFL player mimicked her kangaroo pose while celebrating an interception.
“I was like, ‘Oh no, I’m a meme,” she says in the documentary. “It was this growing monster. Some of the memes were funny and then the tone started to change.
“It really saddened me to see how many women just decided to hate on me,” she continued. “It was a hot topic talking point to just rip into me.”

She felt like the whole thing might blow over by the end of the Olympics, but it showed no signs of stopping. She shared an Instagram video in August 2024 in which she said all the hate had “been pretty devastating.”
Videos started to circulate alleging she cheated her way into an Olympic berth, which the organizer of the Oceania qualifying event shot down as untrue.
“I was cringe,” she says in the documentary. “I brought shame and embarrassment on the country. Yeah, that was rough.”
She says she felt like her whole life was “crumbling” and she was just trying to get through the day. She also was on antidepressants to deal with the anxiety.
What Happened to Raygun After the Olympics?
Gunn and her husband, Sammy Free, say on the Netflix documentary that they took a trip to the Netherlands for two months after the Olympics to lie low in Europe.
Free is a dancer who introduced Gunn to the art form, but her love for breaking had taken a hard turn after Paris.
“I felt like I was falling into a dark pit,” Gunn says in the film.
She called her parents distraught, and she said her father was crying and asking, “Why you? Out of everyone that was there, why you?”
“I realized my life as I know it is over,” Gunn says.
An Unexpected Lifeline
Gunn reveals in the documentary that she received an emotional lift from Richard Branson, the British billionaire and co-founder of the Virgin Group.
Branson reached out to Gunn after watching her Olympic performance and witnessing the backlash.
“In my opinion, she did something extraordinary,” Branson says in the documentary. “She tried something completely original. She stood out from the crowd.”
He invited Gunn and her husband on a cruise, where she danced for an appreciative crowd.
“The idea was that maybe we could change the narrative a bit,” Branson says.
“That was a lifeline to be honest because that really kept me grounded, and I knew I could get through this,” Gunn says.
Where Is Raygun Now?
Two years removed from her Olympic experience, Gunn has rediscovered her love of dancing.

“I’ve been doing little gradual pushes this whole way, and today my goal is just to dance in front of people and to show what happened after Paris hasn’t defeated me,” she says. “I know for sure I’m never going to stop dancing. Time to be a big brave girl and let’s do this.”
The documentary shows her performing in front of a cheering crowd in Taiwan.
Gunn also reveals that she has left her job in academia.
“I’m excited for what’s next,” she says. “I’m open to where this journey may take me.”

title: Katie Holmes Reveals New Boyfriend With First Instagram Post
summary: Katie Holmes appears to have confirmed her romance with rumored boyfriend Jason Bard Yarmosky in an Instagram post.
story: Katie Holmes appears to have confirmed her romance with rumored boyfriend Jason Bard Yarmosky.
On Sept. 1, the “Dawson’s Creek” star posted a pair of pictures on Instagram seeming to indicate they are a couple.
“Happy Birthday to the best of the best…❤️@jasonbardyarmosky,” she captioned a pair of photos.

The first picture features a smiling Holmes holding a microphone while she stands close to Yarmosky with her arm around his waist. The second image is dark and appears to capture a birthday cake with lit candles.
The post was also shared on Yarmosky’s Instagram page.

Holmes also posted a video to her Instagram story in which Yarmosky blows out the candles on his cake while people applaud. Holmes, sitting next to him, gives him a hug, and he kisses her on the forehead.
Rumors that Holmes and Yarmosky were an item had circulated over the last several weeks, as they were seen together at various events during the summer.
Holmes, 47, was previously married to Tom Cruise from 2006 until their divorce in 2012. The couple shares daughter Suri, 20. She was later linked to Jamie Foxx.
Yarmosky works as an artist. His “work centers on themes of aging, time, and memory — subjects the artist has been fascinated with since childhood,” according to his website.

title: Victoria Aveyard Reveals the Opening Scene of Debut Adult Novel, ‘Tempest’
summary: Read the begining of Victoria Aveyard’s new book and adult debut Tempest, the first book in a duology.
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.
Victoria Aveyard first met her latest heroine that same way readers do in the opening lines of her adult fantasy debut, “Tempest”: in a city filled with gallows, staring out at corpses.
Aveyard is a self-proclaimed linear writer, so she always knew how this story would begin.
“Openings for me, at least that initial jump, that’s always quite easy,” Aveyard tells TODAY.com. “I always sort of saw Cat for the first time in my head the way that we see her in the book.”

“Tempest,” out Sept. 8, follows Catrine Rose, a former lady of the Meridian Empire turned pirate tavern owner, in two timelines: before and after. Chapter 1 is firmly set in the “after” and opens with the following scene:
Ships appeared on the endless horizon.

It was hardly an unusual sight in the islands of the Lyrian Sea, where trade winds and swift currents brought countless vessels. Ships of war, ships of trade, ships of passage, ships with no direction at all. Ships of every flag — and none.

Catrine Rose watched in silence from the shore, staring out at the Archenport harbor as it woke up. She looked past the small boats and grander ships, her eyes fixed on the stone arch rising out of the water beyond the docks. Wind and waves and time carved it thus, the white rocks worn smooth, older than living memory. Once the arch had held the black flag, but the Meridian navy burned it upon landing. Now the nooses hung in its stead, the bodies flag enough. Her gaze snagged on the last salt-eaten rope in the line, its loop undone, leaving no trace of the man it once held.
“May the sea always sing for you,” Cat whispered, so low the gentle waves swallowed up her words.

Aveyard has described “Tempest” as an homage to the cinematic high fantasy stories she grew up, such as “Pirates of the Caribbean.” She’s since pitched it to her readers as a “pirate epic” chronicling a “10-year situationship between a fallen lady and a rogue captain.”

The book’s premise establishes that in the “before” timeline, Cat had been married to a “loathsome lord.” But in the after, she lies low as the Widow Rose, working at a tavern until she’s forced, by penalty of death, to track down and capture a pirate from her past, Valerian Kane.

Aveyard wants the first few paragraphs to establish the “violence” of the after timeline — where the pirates that sailed the Lyrian Sea have been wiped out by the Meridian Empire, which Cat once belonged to. She watches the destruction and quietly, passively, prays for them — and herself.

“She’s very much a ghost sort of walking through the echoes of this life that she lived,” Aveyard says. “She knows what this place used to be. She sees what it is now, and she’s sort of caught in the middle. So she’s almost giving up this prayer to the other people who have gone essentially the path that she thinks is going to be set for her as well.”
The image is also meant to illustrate something ending, one that will gain significance the more you read of “Tempest.”

“I want there to be a moment where we’re halfway through the story, we didn’t realize in the moment what this image was really going to do to us, and then we see what the world was and we have this bittersweet sort of recollection of, ‘Wow, I started at the end,’” Aveyard says.

It’s also far from the only time readers will encounter the phrase, “may the sea always sing for you” — it’s printed on the book’s cover, after all. Aveyard says that line hints at a “simmering” mythology under the surface of “Tempest,” which, while originally written as a 1,000+ word standalone, is now a duology. (Book 2, “Tyrant,” is due in summer 2027.)
Months before publication, a TV series adaptation of “Tempest” was announced. Aveyard’s first series, “Red Queen” is currently in development at Peacock.

“I’m just really, really happy,” Aveyard says of how she’s feeling a few days before “Tempest” comes out. “It’s also so validating to have other creatives look at your work, read a book at the manuscript level and say, ‘Hey, we want to go through hell with you to get this to the adaptation.’ It’s a huge vote of confidence.”
Excerpt from TEMPEST by Victoria Aveyard, published by Harper Voyager. Copyright © 2026 by Victoria Aveyard. Reprinted courtesy of HarperCollinsPublishers. Book Link.

title: Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift Have a Dog! And She ‘Crushed’ Her Big Debut in Ad Campaign
summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s dog appears with him in a new ad campaign for Tommy Hilfiger.
story: Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce and their pets are no strangers to getting a round of a-paws.
The couple’s dog is joining those ranks, making her onscreen debut alongside the Kansas City Chiefs tight end in Tommy Hilfiger’s new ad campaign, “Only in New York.”
The pooch is a Samoyed. Kelce confirmed on the Sept. 2 episode of his “New Heights” podcast with his brother, Jason Kelce, that her name is Wendy, and she is a little over a year old.
“Wendy is, she is officially a picture dog,” Travis Kelce said while discussing her work in the shoot.
The Hilfiger team had mulled over including a dog in the campaign, and Kelce thought his and Swift’s pup would be a natural, so he said he talked it over with her.

“She was all for it. And it’s it’s kind of crazy how perfect (Wendy) looks in a Tommy Hilfiger world, you know what I mean?” he said. “She matches the brand and the shoot, and it was pretty easy to get her to jump on the couch and have some fun with us. So ... Wendy’s now a model.”
In one clip from the ad, Kelce arrives to his room at New York City’s Plaza Hotel and sits with the dog on a couch, where the animal enjoys getting pet and frolics on the furniture.
The pair also hang out on a couch in another clip. Kelce shared the ad to his own Instagram page and noted in the caption, “There’s also one very special cameo in there too.”
Another image from the campaign captures the dog with a paw wrapped around Kelce’s left leg, tongue out.
The campaign also stars Gigi Hadid, musicians Jisoo and Peggy Gou, and athletes Frances Tiafoe and Carmelo Anthony.
Kelce, who married Swift on July 3 at Madison Square Garden, said he was thrilled to be part of Hilfiger’s New York-set campaign.

“Tommy brought us into his world at The Plaza for this, and it doesn’t get more classic New York than that,” he said in a statement. “There’s a magic to this city, and I love that you never know who or what’s around the corner. We had a blast tapping into that unique energy with a cast who truly embody the vibes that make this city so special.”
Swift is famously the owner of three cats, Olivia Benson, Meredith Grey and Benjamin Button, who have all had their own moment in the spotlight.

Olivia, named after Mariska Hargitay’s character on “Law & Order: SVU,” appeared in a Keds commercial in 2014. (Hargitay would later name her cat Karma, in honor of Swift’s track from the “Midnight”s album.) Both Olivia and Meredith appeared in a 2018 commercial for DirecTV, and in 2023, Benjamin appeared on the cover of Time when Swift was named Person of the Year.

title: Savannah Guthrie Teams Up With Jimmy Fallon to Double ‘Password’ Winners’ Prize
summary: The latest celeb guest on “Password” is none other than TODAY’s Savannah Guthrie!
story: The latest celeb guest on “Password” is none other than TODAY’s Savannah Guthrie!

Savannah appeared on two episodes of the NBC game show that aired Sept. 1 alongside Jimmy Fallon and host Keke Palmer. In both episodes, Savannah showed off her impressive guessing skills while helping each contestant earn enough points to make it to the next round and eventually compete for the grand prize of $25,000.

The TODAY co-host practically bounced onto the set when Palmer introduced her in the first episode, titled “Like Nails on a Chalkboard.” After Fallon shared a fun fact about his contestant, Justin, Savannah gave her contestant, Kia, a warm welcome. She revealed that Kia is a minister of 20 years.
Kia explained that as a minister she likes to “encourage people to use their gift and walk in their calling.” She also said that she met her husband at church.
“He was supposed to be looking at the minister, but instead he was looking at me. And I was looking at him back,” she cheekily said.

After their first round as a pair, Savannah and Kia took the lead. For round two, the clue was the title of the episode, meaning that all the passwords were words “that make you cover your ears.” Savannah and Fallon swapped partners, and Kia won again, securing a spot in the “Bonus Round.”
For the last round, Kia had to get Savannah and Fallon to correctly guess 10 passwords. But, they only gave nine right answers, which earned Kia $9,000.

Kia then had one final chance to double her money. She was given a secret password and could only share one clue with Savannah and Fallon. Her clue was guacamole. Fallon and Savannah correctly figured out the password was avocado. Kia celebrated with the duo and left the show $18,000 richer.

For part two, titled “What Beats Scissors,” Savannah returned to team up with Chantae and Michael. Her first partner was Michael, who Savannah revealed recently got engaged. Michael shared that he popped the question to his partner Christopher of eight years during a trip to England. “I pulled a ring out and I said some nice things and he said ‘yes,’” he gushed.

By the end of round one, Savannah and Michael led Fallon and Chantae 16 to 9. In round two, the title of the episode once again became the clue as all the passwords were answers “that rock.” Although Savannah and Chantae briefly grabbed the lead, Fallon and Michael took the victory.
In the “Bonus Round,” Michael struggled and the hopes of winning $25,000 disappeared. However, he still won $8,000 and was able to double his winnings.
When Michael delivered his final clue of “sweep,” Savannah and Fallon instantly knew that the last password was “chimney.”
They were right and Michael hugged the two before walking away with $16,000.
Savannah and Fallon cheered, successfully helping two contestants double their cash prize.

The game show experience will come in handy for Savannah, who will soon host the upcoming “Wordle” competition series inspired by the popular puzzle game. Her new show is set to premiere on NBC in 2027.

title: Carole Radziwill Speaks on Epstein Files Ahead of ‘RHONY’ New Season: ‘It’s Important to Talk About It’
summary: Carole Radziwill is addressing being one of the many public figures whose name appeared in the millions of files released by the Department of Justice regarding the Jeffrey Epstein investigation.
story: Carole Radziwill is addressing being one of the many public figures whose name appeared in the millions of files released by the Department of Justice regarding the Jeffrey Epstein investigation.

The author and “Real Housewives of New York City” star, who rejoined the series for its upcoming Season 16 after stepping away from the show in 2018, spoke about the files during a Bravo press event held at the Wölffer Estate Vineyard in Sagaponack, New York, on Sept. 1.

At the event, Radziwill was asked by Bravo’s Andy Cohen about her return to the franchise. He recalled a conversation with Radziwill in which she said that rejoining the show felt like an “opportunity” after her name appeared in the Epstein files.

“I mean, I felt like this isn’t something I shy away from,” she said. “Me and many, many, many, many more people found their names in these files. And it’s not something I shy away from because I think, really, it’s important to talk about it. It’s important to be transparent. Obviously, I didn’t know anything, as no one, you know, 20 years ago would have known anything.”

Radziwill, a former TV news producer who was married to John F. Kennedy Jr.’s cousin and best friend, the late Anthony Radziwill, has said she did not know Epstein. In a March interview with The New York Times, Radziwill said she was friends with Ghislaine Maxwell, convicted co-conspirator of Epstein, in the early 2000s for “five or six years.” Maxwell did not speak to her about Epstein, she told the Times.
“It’s hard to think that someone you knew that long ago, even called a friend at some point, was a horrible, horrible person doing horrible things,” Radziwill said at the Sept. 1 event.
The release of the files made her nervous at first, she said, but later believed it was an opportunity to talk about it.
“There (are) real victims and survivors that were brave enough to really stand up to these very, very powerful people,” she said.

Radziwill appears to address the Epstein files on the new season of “RHONY”; a trailer for Season 16, premiering on Bravo Sept. 8, sees Radziwill when confronted with questions from a fellow cast member.

title: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ Announcer Jim Thornton Suspended From Show
summary: “Wheel of Fortune” longtime announcer Jim Thornton has been suspended from the show and his role will be recast, TODAY.com has learned.
story: “Wheel of Fortune” longtime announcer Jim Thornton has been suspended from the show and his role will be recast, TODAY.com has learned.
Sony Pictures Television Studios confirmed in a statement sent to TODAY.com Tuesday, Sept. 1, that Thornton will not be involved with the show as the studio looks into allegations against him.

“We have recently been made aware of allegations concerning Jim Thornton. He has been suspended from ‘Wheel of Fortune’ and we are recasting while we conduct a thorough investigation,” the studio said.
The studio did not share more details about the allegations or investigation.
TODAY.com has reached out to Thornton for a comment.
TMZ was first to report the news of Thornton’s suspension. The outlet also reported that the allegations involve an incident between Thornton and an American Airlines passenger on a flight in May.
In a statement to TODAY.com, American Airlines did not mention Thornton by name. However, the airline did confirm there was an incident on a flight in May.

“On ​May 14, ​American Airlines ​Flight ​1276 ​was met by ​law enforcement ​upon ​arrival at ​Los ​Angeles ​International ​Airport ​(LAX) following concerns reported by a customer ​onboard,” the statement said.
Thornton, 66, has been the voice of “Wheel of Fortune” since 2010, the same year original announcer Charlie O’Donnell died at the age of 78.

Thornton was initially a guest announcer, according to IMDb, and officially joined the show as the main announcer for its 29th season in 2011. He has announced a total of 2980 episodes and has also served as an announcer for “Celebrity Wheel of Fortune” since 2021.
His voice acting credits include roles in “The Cleveland Show,” “Celebrity Deathmatch” and “Monsters, Inc.” as well.

Thornton has spent most of his time on “Wheel of Fortune” behind the cameras, with Pat Sajak and Vanna White serving as the hosts until Sajak’s departure in June 2024. Ryan Seacrest began hosting the game show with White in September 2024.

title: ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ Crowns Winner After Dynamic and Emotional Finale
summary: During the “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro” finale, one dancer was crowned the winner and the new pro for Season 35 of “DWTS.”
story: There’s officially a new pro entering the “Dancing With the Stars” world.
After weeks of challenges and testing their dancing, teaching and interpersonal skills on and off the ballroom floor, one performer was named the winner of “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro.”
During the Aug. 31 finale, the final three contestants — Adele Zaikman, AJ Pritchard and Selena Hamilton — were tasked with a final challenge: dancing with a star.
Derek Hough returned as guest judge alongside Mark and Shirley Ballas, while Witney Carson co-hosted with Robert Irwin.

The “DWTS: The Next Pro” finale kicked off with a dynamic performance by the dance troupe, as well as Mark and Shirley dancing together. They were also joined by Derek, while Robert got a chance to once again show off his talents on the dance floor alongside his former champion partner Witney.
The opening ended with the three finalists joining the judges and hosts for a sequence worthy of a “DWTS” finale.

Kicking off the competition, which was held in front of a live audience, AJ, Adele and Selena were partnered with former “Dancing with the Stars” finalists Charli D’Amelio, Nēv Schulman and Adam Rippon, respectively, to perform two dances.

In the first round, the finalists would be able to choose their favorite ballroom or Latin style to really impress the judges. In the second round, just like on “DWTS,” they would be performing a freestyle.
What Happened During the ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ Finale?

Selena and Adam were up first and performed a jive together. During rehearsals, the two appeared to work perfectly together, which was evident by their energy-filled performance. Mark called Selena an “electric” dancer and loved the kick, kick, Pas de Bourrée sequence. However, he did note he was left wanting more. Shirley called Selena “Miss Wow” and praised her ability to take direction, while Derek said she “commands attention” and is a star.

While rehearing AJ made sure Charlie felt comfortable in his arms while dancing the Viennese waltz. That was made evident in their performance. Mark began by praising his former partner, before complimenting AJ as a “fantastic” ballroom dancer. While there were some moments at the end that needed tweaking, he called it a “really solid performance.” Derek echoed the sentiments, applauding their trust. Shirley noted that AJ’s technique was on point but questioned if he had enough “wow moments” with Charlie.

Up next were Adele and Nēv with a samba. During rehearsals she noted that it was the “hardest” Latin ballroom style and wasn’t aware she’d be teaching someone who had never danced samba before. Nēv, on his end, was experiencing jet lag, which prompted Adele to end their first day early. However, the judges gave their routine a standing ovation with Derek calling it Nēv’s “redemption.” The judge did note that the routine needed more creativity, but the quality was there. Mark said the “Queen cobra struck again,” yet when it came to Nēv he wished he would’ve seen him go “wild, crazy” and let loose a bit more. Shirley called Adele a “magical teacher” and said “well done” to both of them.
Before the second round, the trio reflected on what led them to pursue a career in dance and what fueled their passion. Then it was freestyle time.

Selena described her routine with Adam as “gritty, contemporary fusion.” Their performance to “Cry Me a River” was met with an “oh my God” from Shirley mid-routine. After a standing ovation from the judges, Mark said he loved the dangerous opening and the various standout moments. Shirley noted that if this was on “DWTS” it would be “ranked as one of the best” routines she’s seen, calling Selena “one of a kind.” Derek, on his end, was a fan of the choreography, execution, musicality and confidence they brought to the ballroom. He said if she was on “DWTS,” she would be a “fan favorite.”

For AJ and Charlie’s final routine, he wanted to celebrate his “Next Pro” experience by including everything he learned over the last weeks. Filled with plenty of wow moments, the routine had the judges on their feet. Shirley congratulated AJ for “going big” and jam-packing the dance with a slew of epic and fun moments. Derek said the freestyle “had it all” and challenged Charlie in the best way. Mark, on his end, commended AJ on putting together a grandiose routine in such a short amount of time.

Last but not least Adele chose a paso doble “with a twist” for her and Nēv’s freestyle. Finishing strong with a standing ovation, Derek said the routine was “on fire, pun intended,” powerful and stood out from the others. Mark admired all the ballroom elements Adele incorporated, calling it “captivating.” Shirley appreciated that Adele makes her “partners work hard” and called both of her routines “excellent.”
Who Won ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’?
After eight weeks of intense competition and their two final dances, it was time to learn who would be landing the coveted “DWTS” pro spot for Season 35.
In third place was Selena, who said she didn’t think she would make it past the first week. “This is not the end,” she said, grateful for the experience and friendships.
In second place was AJ, who said he was “absolutely devastated from every being in my body,” but called his journey “enriching.”
Which meant Adele was crowned “The Next Pro.” In tears, she called this “a celebration” of all the sacrifices she’s made over the years.
What Happens Next?
Now, the new winner will get their chance to be part of “Dancing With the Stars” Season 35, which will premiere on Sept. 15.
Fans will have to wait a couple of days to find out which celebrity Adele will be paired with when the full cast is announced on Sept. 2.

title: Oil touches $97 per barrel as diesel prices surge to highest level this year
summary: The nationwide average price for diesel fuel rose to $5.78 per gallon, up 9 cents overnight.
story: A monthlong run of rising crude oil prices and refineries’ nearing capacity has pushed the average cost of diesel fuel to its highest since 2022.
At $5.78 per gallon Thursday, the cost of diesel is up more than 53% since the war with Iran started in late February. At the time, it was $3.76 nationwide.

The price of unleaded gasoline, which most personal vehicles run on, rose alongside diesel Thursday. According to AAA data tracked by NBC News, the national average was $4.14 per gallon, up 2 cents from Wednesday.

title: U.S. strikes 3 Iranian oil tankers after Iran targets Navy warships, military says
summary: U.S. forces struck three Iranian oil tankers Saturday after Iran launched ballistic missiles toward two U.S.
story: U.S. forces struck three Iranian oil tankers Saturday after Iran launched ballistic missiles toward two U.S. Navy ships, the U.S. military said.
A U.S. aircraft carrier and guided missile destroyer evaded multiple attacks by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, U.S. Central Command said in a statement. No American personnel were harmed.

CENTCOM said U.S. forces retaliated by permanently disabling two crude oil carriers, the M/T Downy off the coast of Kharg Island and the M/T Stark 1 near Jask. Forces also destroyed a third vessel, the M/T Kylo near the Gulf of Oman.
The Kylo was not carrying oil at the time and its crew was directed to abandon the vessel before American forces struck it in multiple locations, CENTCOM said.

“If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours,” Adm. Brad Cooper, the commander of CENTCOM, said in a statement. “We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet.”
